22:55.t: But the Infidels will not cease to doubt concerning it, until "the Hour" come suddenly upon them, or until the chastisement of the day of desolation come upon them

22:56.t: On that day the Kingdom shall be God's: He shall judge between them: and they who shall have believed and done the things that are right, shall be in gardens of delight

22:57.t: But they who were Infidels and treated our signs as lies - these then - their's a shameful chastisement

22:58.t: And as to those who fled their country for the cause of God, and were afterwards slain, or died, surely with goodly provision will God provide for them! for verily, God! He, surely, is the best of providers

22:59.t: He will assuredly bring them in with an in-bringing that shall please them well: for verily, God is right Knowing, Gracious

22:60.t: So shall it be. And whoever in making exact reprisal for injury done him, shall again be wronged, God will assuredly aid him: for God is most Merciful, Gracious

22:61.t: So shall it be; for that God causeth the night to enter in upon the day, and He causeth the day to enter in upon the night: and for that God Heareth, Seeth

22:62.t: So shall it be, for that God is the truth; and because what they call on beside Him is vanity: and because God is the Lofty, the Mighty

22:63.t: Seest thou not that God sendeth down water from Heaven, and that on the morrow the earth is clad with verdure? for God is benignant, cognisant of all

22:64.t: His, all in the Heavens and all on Earth: and verily, God! He assuredly is the Rich, the Praiseworthy

22:65.t: Seest thou not that God hath put under you whatever is in the earth; and the ships which traverse the sea at His bidding? And He holdeth back the heaven that it fall not on the earth, unless He permit it! for God is right Gracious to mankind, Merciful

22:66.t: And He it is who hath given you life, then will cause you to die, then will give you life - of a truth man is all ungrateful

22:67.t: To every people have we appointed observances which they observe. Therefore, let them not dispute this matter with thee, but bid them to thy Lord, for thou art on the right way

22:68.t: But if they debate with thee, then Say: God best knoweth what ye do

22:69.t: God will judge between you on the day of resurrection, as to the matters wherein ye differ

22:70.t: Knowest thou not that God knoweth whatever is in the Heaven and on the Earth? This truly is written in the Book: this truly is easy for God

22:71.t: They worship beside God, that for which He hath sent down no warranty, and that of which they have no knowledge: but for those who commit this wrong, no helper

22:72.t: And when our clear signs are rehearsed to them, thou mayst perceive disdain in the countenances of the Infidels. Scarce can they refrain from rushing to attack those who rehearse our signs to them! SAY: Shall I tell you of worse than this? The fire which God hath threatened to those who believe not! Wretched the passage thither

22:73.t: O men! a parable is set forth to you, wherefore hearken to it. Verily, they on whom ye call beside God, cannot create a fly, though they assemble for it; and if the fly carry off aught from them, they cannot take it away from it! Weak the suppliant and the supplicated

22:74.t: Unworthy the estimate they form of God! for God is right Powerful, Mighty

22:75.t: God chooseth messengers from among the angels and from among men: verily, God Heareth, Seeth

22:76.t: He knoweth what is before them and what is behind them; and unto God shall all things return

22:77.t: Believers! bow down and prostrate yourselves and worship your Lord, and work righteousness that you may fare well

22:78.t: And do valiantly in the cause of God as it behoveth you to do for Him. He hath elected you, and hath not laid on you any hardship in religion, the Faith of your father Abraham. He hath named you the Muslims Heretofore and in this Book, that the Apostles may be a witness against you, and that ye may be witnesses against the rest of mankind. Therefore observe prayer, and pay the legal impost, and cleave fast to God. He is your liege Lord - a goodly Lord, and a goodly Helper

23:2.t: Who humble them in their prayer

23:3.t: And who keep aloof from vain words

23:4.t: And who are doers of alms deeds

23:6.t: Save with their wives, or the slaves whom their right hands possess: for in that case they shall be free from blame

23:7.t: But they whose desires reach further than this are transgressors

23:8.t: And who tend well their trusts and their covenants

23:9.t: And who keep them strictly to their prayers

23:11.t: Who shall inherit the paradise, to abide therein for ever

23:12.t: Now of fine clay have we created man

23:13.t: Then we placed him, a moist germ, in a safe abode

23:14.t: Then made we the moist germ a clot of blood: then made the clotted blood into a piece of flesh; then made the piece of flesh into bones: and we clothed the bones with flesh: then brought forth man of yet another make - Blessed therefore be God, the most excellent of Makers

23:15.t: Then after this ye shall surely die

23:16.t: Then shall ye be waked up on the day of resurrection

23:17.t: And we have created over you seven heavens: - and we are not careless of the creation

23:18.t: And we send down water from the Heaven in its due degree, and we cause it to settle on the earth; - and we have power for its withdrawal

23:19.t: And by it we cause gardens of palm trees, and vineyards to spring forth for you, in which ye have plenteous fruits, and whereof ye eat

23:20.t: And the tree that groweth up on Mount Sinai; which yieldeth oil and a juice for those who eat

23:21.t: And there is a lesson for you in the cattle: We give you to drink of what is in their bellies, and many advantages do ye derive from them, and for food they serve you

23:22.t: And on them and on ships are ye borne

23:23.t: We sent Noah heretofore unto his people, and he said, "O my people! serve God: ye have no other God than He: will ye not therefore fear Him

23:24.t: But the chiefs of the people who believed not said, "This is but a man like yourselves: he fain would raise himself above you: but had it pleased God to send, He would have sent angels: We heard not of this with our sires of old

23:25.t: Verily he is but a man possessed; leave him alone therefore for a time

23:26.t: He said, "O my Lord! help me against their charge of imposture

23:27.t: So we revealed unto him, "Make the ark under our eye, and as we have taught, and when our doom shall come on, and the earth's surface shall boil up, Carry into it of every kind a pair, and thy family, save him on whom sentence hath already passed: and plead not with me for the wicked, for they shall be drowned

23:28.t: And when thou, and they who shall be with thee, shall go up into the ark; say, 'Praise be unto God, who hath rescued us from the wicked folk

23:29.t: And say, 'O my Lord! disembark me with a blessed disembarking: for thou art the best to disembark

23:30.t: Verily in this were signs, and verily we made proof of man

23:31.t: We then raised up other generations after them

23:32.t: And we sent among them an apostle from out themselves, with, "Worship ye God! ye have no other God than He: will ye not therefore fear Him

23:33.t: And the chiefs of His people who believed not, and who deemed the meeting with us in the life to come to be a lie, and whom we had richly supplied in this present life, said, "This is but a man like yourselves; he eateth of what ye eat, And he drinketh of what ye drink

23:34.t: And if ye obey a man like yourselves, then ye will surely be undone

23:35.t: What! doth he foretell you, that after ye shall be dead and become dust and bones, ye shall be brought forth

23:37.t: There is no life beyond our present life; we die, and we live, and we shall not be quickened again

23:38.t: This is merely a man who forgeth a lie about God: and we will not believe him

23:39.t: He said, "O my Lord! help me against this charge of imposture

23:40.t: He said, "Yet a little, and they will soon repent them

23:41.t: Then did the shout of the destroying angel in justice surprise them, we made them like leaves swept down by a torrent. Away then with the wicked people

23:42.t: Then raised we up other generations after them

23:43.t: Neither too soon, nor too late, shall a people reach its appointed time

23:44.t: Then sent we our apostles one after another. Oft as their apostle presented himself to a nation, they treated him as a liar; and we caused one nation to follow another; and we made them the burden of a tale. Away then with the people who believe not

23:45.t: Then sent we Moses and his brother Aaron, with our signs and manifest power

23:46.t: To Pharaoh and his princes; but they behaved them proudly, for they were a haughty people

23:47.t: And they said, "Shall we believe on two men like ourselves, whose people are our slaves

23:48.t: And they treated them both as impostors; wherefore they became of the destroyed

23:49.t: And we gave Moses the Book for Israel's guidance

23:50.t: And we appointed the Son of Mary, and His mother for a sign; and we prepared an abode for both in a lofty spot, quiet, and watered with springs

23:51.t: O ye apostles! eat of things that are good: and do that which is right: of your doings I am cognisant

23:52.t: And truly this your religion is the one religion; and I am your Lord: therefore fear me

23:53.t: But men have rent their great concern, one among another, into sects; every party rejoicing in that which is their own

23:54.t: Wherefore leave them till a certain time, in their depths of error

23:55.t: What! think they that what we largely, bestow on them of wealth and children

23:56.t: We hasten to them for their good? Nay, they have no knowledge

23:57.t: But they who are awed with the dread of their Lord

23:58.t: And who believe in the signs of their Lord

23:59.t: And who join no other gods with their Lord

23:60.t: And who give that which they give with hearts thrilled with dread because they must return unto their Lord

23:61.t: These hasten after good, and are the first to win it

23:62.t: We will not burden a soul beyond its power: and with us is a book, which speaketh the truth; and they shall not be wronged

23:63.t: But as to this Book, their hearts are plunged in error, and their works are far other than those of Muslims, and they will work those works

23:64.t: Until when we lay hold on their affluent ones with punishment; lo! they cry for help

23:65.t: Cry not for help this day, for by Us ye shall not be succoured

23:66.t: Long since were my signs rehearsed to you, but ye turned back on your heels

23:67.t: Puffed up with pride, discoursing foolishly by night

23:68.t: Do they not then heed the things spoken - whether that hath come to them which came not to their fathers of old

23:69.t: Or do they not recognise their apostle; and therefore disavow him

23:70.t: Or say they, "A Djinn is in him?" Nay! he hath come to them with the truth; but the truth do most of them abhor

23:71.t: But if the truth had followed in the train of their desires, the heavens and the earth, and all that therein is, had surely come to ruin! But we have brought them their warning; and from their warning they withdraw

23:72.t: Dost thou ask them for remuneration? But, remuneration from thy Lord is best; and He is the best provider

23:73.t: And thou indeed biddest them to the right path

23:74.t: But verily they who believe not in the life to come, from that path do surely wander

23:75.t: And if we had taken compassion on them, and relieved them from their trouble, they would have plunged on in their wickedness, wildly wandering

23:76.t: We formerly laid hold on them with chastisement, yet they did not humble them to their Lord, nor did they abase them

23:77.t: Until, when we have opened upon them the door of a severe punishment, lo! they are in despair at it

23:78.t: It is He who hath implanted in you hearing, and sight, and heart; how few of you give thanks

23:79.t: It is He who hath caused you to be born on the earth: and unto Him shall ye be gathered

23:80.t: And it is He who maketh alive and killeth, and of Him is the change of the night and of the day: Will ye not understand

23:81.t: But they say, as said those of old

23:82.t: They say,"What! When we shall be dead, and have become dust and bones, shall we, indeed, be waked to life

23:83.t: This have we been promised, we and our fathers aforetime: but it is only fables of the ancients

23:84.t: SAY: Whose is the earth, and all that is therein; - if ye know

23:85.t: They will answer, "God's." SAY: Will ye not, then reflect

23:86.t: SAY: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens, and the Lord of the glorious throne

23:87.t: They will say, "They are God's". SAY: Will ye not, then, fear Him

23:88.t: SAY: In whose hand is the empire of all things, who protecteth but is not protected? if ye know

23:89.t: They will answer, "In God's." SAY: How, then, can ye be so spell-bound

23:90.t: Yea, we have brought them the truth; but they are surely liars

23:91.t: God hath not begotten offspring; neither is there any other God with Him: else had each god assuredly taken away that which he had created, and some had assuredly uplifted themselves above others! Far from the glory of God, be what they affirm of Him

23:92.t: He knoweth alike the unseen and the seen: far be He uplifted above the gods whom they associate with Him

23:93.t: SAY: O my Lord! If thou wilt let me witness the infliction of that with which they have been threatened

23:94.t: O my Lord! place me not among the ungodly people

23:95.t: Verily, we are well able to make thee see the punishment with which we have threatened them

23:96.t: Turn aside evil with that which is better: we best know what they utter against thee

23:97.t: And SAY: "O my Lord! I betake me to Thee, against the promptings of the Satans

23:98.t: And I betake me to Thee, O my Lord! that they gain no hurtful access to me

23:99.t: When death overtaketh one of the wicked, he saith, "Lord, send me back again

23:100.t: That I may do the good which I have left undone." "By no means." These are the very words which he shall speak: But behind them shall be a barrier, until the day when they shall be raised again

23:101.t: And when the trumpet shall be sounded, the ties of kindred between them shall cease on that day; neither shall they ask each other's help

23:102.t: They whose balances shall be heavy, shall be the blest

23:103.t: But they whose balances shall be light, - these are they who shall lose their souls, abiding in hell for ever

23:104.t: The fire shall scorch their faces, and their lips shall quiver therein

23:105.t: What! Were not my signs rehearsed unto you? and did ye not treat them as lies

23:106.t: They shall say, "O our Lord! our ill-fortune prevailed against us, and we became an erring people

23:107.t: O our Lord! Bring us forth hence: if we go back again to our sins, we shall indeed be evil doers

23:108.t: He will say; "Be ye driven down into it; and, address me not

23:109.t: A part truly of my servants was there, who said, "O our Lord! we believe: forgive us, then, and be merciful to us, for of the merciful art thou the best

23:110.t: But ye received them with such scoffs that they suffered you to forget my warning, and ye laughed them to scorn

23:111.t: Verily this day will I reward then, for their patient endurance: the blissful ones shall they be

23:112.t: He will say, "What number of years tarried ye on earth

23:113.t: They will say, "We tarried a day, or part of a day; but ask the recording angels

23:114.t: God will say, "Short indeed was the time ye tarried, if that ye knew it

23:115.t: What! Did ye then think that we had created you for pastime, and that ye should not be brought back again to us

23:116.t: Wherefore let God be exalted, the King, the Truth! There is no god but He! Lord of the stately throne

23:117.t: And whoso, together with God, shall call on another god, for whom he hath no proof, shall surely have to give account to his Lord. Aye, it shall fare ill with the infidels

23:118.t: And SAY: "O my Lord, pardon, and have mercy; for of those who show mercy, art thou the best

24:1.t: A SURA which we have sent down and sanctioned! Clear signs have we sent down therein, that ye may take warning

24:2.t: The whore and the whoremonger - scourge each of them with an hundred stripes; and let not compassion keep you from carrying out the sentence of God, if ye believe in God and the last day: And let some of the faithful witness their chastisement

24:3.t: The whoremonger shall not marry other than a whore or an idolatress; and the whore shall not marry other than a whoremonger or an idolater. Such alliances are forbidden to the faithful

24:4.t: They who defame virtuous women, and bring not four witnesses, scourge them with fourscore stripes, and receive ye not their testimony for ever, for these are perverse persons

24:5.t: Save those who afterwards repent and live virtuously; for truly God is Lenient, Merciful

24:6.t: And they who shall accuse their wives, and have no witnesses but themselves, the testimony of each of them shall be a testimony by God four times repeated, that he is indeed of them that speak the truth

24:7.t: And the fifth time that the malison of God be upon him, if he be of them that lie

24:8.t: But it shall avert the chastisement from her if she testify a testimony four times repeated, by God, that he is of them that lie

24:9.t: And a fifth time to call down the wrath of God on her, if he have spoken the truth

24:10.t: And but for the goodness and mercy of God towards you, and that God is He who loveth to turn, Wise

24:11.t: Of a truth, they who advanced that lie were a large number of you; but regard it not as an evil to you. No, it is an advantage to you. To every man among them shall it be done according to the offence he hath committed; and as to that person among them who took on himself to aggravate it, a sore punishment doth await him

24:12.t: Did not the faithful of both sexes, when ye heard of this, form a favourable judgment in their own minds, and say, "This is a manifest lie

24:13.t: Have they brought four witnesses of the fact? If they cannot produce the witnesses, they are the liars in the sight of God

24:14.t: And but for the goodness of God towards you, and His mercy in this world and in the next, a severe punishment had come upon you for that which ye spread abroad

24:15.t: when ye uttered with your tongues, and spake with your mouths that of which ye had no knowledge. Ye deemed it to be a light matter, but with God it was a grave one

24:16.t: And did ye say when ye heard it, "It is not for us to talk of this affair! O God! By thy Glory, this is a gross calumny

24:17.t: God hath warned you that ye go not back to the like of this for ever, if ye be believers

24:18.t: And God maketh His signs clear to you: for God is Knowing, Wise

24:19.t: But as for those who love that foul calumnies should go forth against those who believe, a grievous chastisement awaits them In this world and in the next. And God hath knowledge, but ye have not

24:20.t: And but for the goodness of God towards you and His Mercy, and that God is Kind, Merciful

24:21.t: O ye who believe! follow not the steps of Satan, for whosoever shall follow the steps of Satan, he will enjoin on him what is base and blameworthy; and but for the goodness of God towards you, and His mercy, no one of you had been cleansed for ever: but God maketh whom He will to be clean, and God Heareth, Knoweth

24:22.t: And let not persons of wealth and means among you swear that they will not give to their kindred, to the poor, and to those who have fled their homes in the cause of God; let them rather pardon and pass over the offence. Desire ye not that God should forgive you? And God is Gracious, Merciful

24:23.t: Verily, they who throw out charges against virtuous but careless women, who yet are believers, shall be cursed in this world and in the world to come; and a terrible punishment doth await them

24:24.t: Their own tongues, and hands, and feet, shall one day bear witness against them of their own doings

24:25.t: On that day will God pay them their just due, and they shall know that God is the clear Truth itself

24:26.t: Bad women for bad men, and bad men for bad women; but virtuous women for virtuous men, and virtuous men for virtuous women! These shall be cleared from calumnies; theirs shall be forgiveness and an honourable provision

24:27.t: O ye who believe! enter not into other houses than your own, until ye have asked leave, and have saluted its inmates. This will be best for you: haply ye will bear this in mind

24:28.t: And if ye find no one therein, then enter it not till leave be given you; and if it be said to you, "Go ye back," then go ye back. This will be more blameless in you, and God knoweth what ye do

24:29.t: There shall be no harm in your entering houses in which no one dwelleth, for the supply of your needs: and God knoweth what ye do openly and what ye hide

24:30.t: Speak unto the believers that they restrain their eyes and observe continence. Thus will they be more pure. God is well aware of what they do

24:31.t: And speak to the believing women that they refrain their eyes, and observe continence; and that they display not their ornaments, except those which are external; and that they throw their veils over their bosoms, and display not their ornaments, except to their husbands or their fathers, or their husbands' fathers, or their sons, or their husbands' sons, or their brothers, or their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons, or their women, or their slaves, or male domestics who have no natural force, or to children who note not women's nakedness. And let them not strike their feet together, so as to discover their hidden ornaments. And be ye all turned to God, O ye Believers! that it may be well with you

24:32.t: And marry those among you who are single, and your good servants, and the handmaidens. If they are poor, God of His bounty will enrich them. God is all-bounteous, Knowing

24:33.t: And let those who cannot find a match live in continence till God of His bounty shall enrich them. And to those of your slaves who desire a deed of manumission, execute it for them, if ye know good in them, and give them a portion of the wealth of God which He hath given you. Force not your female slaves into sin, in order that ye may gain the casual fruitions of this world, if they wish to preserve their modesty. Yet if any one compel them, then Verily to them, after their compulsion, will God be Forgiving, Merciful

24:34.t: And now have we sent down to you clear signs, and an instance from among those who flourished before you, and a caution for the God-fearing

24:35.t: God is the LIGHT of the Heavens and of the Earth. His Light is like a niche in which is a lamp - the lamp encased in glass - the glass, as it were, a glistening star. From a blessed tree is it lighted, the olive neither of the East nor of the West, whose oil would well nigh shine out, even though fire touched it not! It is light upon light. God guideth whom He will to His light, and God setteth forth parables to men, for God knoweth all things

24:36.t: In the temples which God hath allowed to be reared, that His name may therein be remembered, do men praise Him morn and even

24:37.t: Men whom neither merchandise nor traffic beguile from the remembrance of God, and from the observance of prayer, and the payment of the stated alms, through fear of the day when hearts shall throb and eyes shall roll

24:38.t: That for their most excellent works may God recompense them, and of His bounty increase it to them more and more: for God maketh provision for whom He pleaseth without measure

24:39.t: But as to the infidels, their works are like the vapour in a plain which the thirsty dreameth to be water, until when he cometh unto it, he findeth it not aught, but findeth that God is with him; and He fully payeth him his account: for swift to take account is God

24:40.t: Or like the darkness on the deep sea when covered by billows riding upon billows, above which are clouds: darkness upon darkness. When a man reacheth forth his hand, he cannot nearly see it! He to whom God shall not give light, no light at all hath he

24:41.t: Hast thou not seen how all in the Heavens and in the Earth uttereth the praise of God? - the very birds as they spread their wings? Every creature knoweth its prayer and its praise! and God knoweth what they do

24:42.t: God's, the Kingdom of the Heavens and of the Earth: and unto God the final return

24:43.t: Hast thou not seen that God driveth clouds lightly forward, then gathereth them together, then pileth them in masses? And then thou seest the rain forthcoming from their midst; and He causeth clouds like mountains charged with hail, to descend from the heaven, and He maketh it to fall on whom He will, and from whom He will He turneth it aside. - The brightness of His lightning all but taketh away the sight

24:44.t: God causeth the day and the night to take their turn. Verily in this is teaching for men of insight

24:45.t: And God hath created every animal of water. Some go upon the belly; some go upon two feet; some go upon four feet. God hath created what He pleased. Aye, God hath power over all things

24:46.t: Now have we sent down distinct signs. - And God guideth whom He will into the right path

24:47.t: For there are who say "We believe on God and on the Apostle, and we obey;" yet, after this, a part of them turn back. But these are not of the faithful

24:48.t: And when they are summoned before God and His Apostle that He may judge between them, lo! a part of them withdraw

24:49.t: But had the truth been on their side, they would have come to Him, obedient

24:50.t: What! are they diseased of heart? Do they doubt? Are they afraid that God and His Apostles will deal unfairly with them? Nay, themselves are the unjust doers

24:51.t: The words of the believers, when called to God and His Apostle that He may judge between them, are only to say, "We have heard, and we obey:" these are they with whom it shall be well

24:52.t: And whoso shall obey God, and His Apostle, and shall dread God and fear Him, these are they that shall be the blissful

24:53.t: And they have sworn by God, with a most solemn oath, that if thou give them the word, they will certainly march forth. Say: swear ye not: of more worth is obedience. Verily, God is well aware of what ye do

24:54.t: SAY: Obey God and obey the Apostle. Suppose that ye turn back, still the burden of his duty is on him only, and the burden of your duty rests on you. If ye obey Him, ye shall have guidance: but plain preaching is all that devolves upon the Apostle

24:55.t: God hath promised to those of you who believe and do the things that are right, that He will cause them to succeed others in the land, as He gave succession to those who were before them, and that He will establish for them that religion which they delight in, and that after their fears He will give them security in exchange. They shall worship Me: nought shall they join with Me: And whoso, after this, believe not, they will be the impious

24:56.t: But observe prayer, and pay the stated alms, and obey the Apostle, that haply ye may find mercy

24:57.t: Let not the Infidels think that they can weaken God on His own Earth: their dwelling place shall be the Fire! and right wretched the journey

24:58.t: O ye who believe! let your slaves, and those of you who have not come of age, ask leave of you, three times a day, ere they come into your presence; - before the morning prayer, and when ye lay aside your garments at mid-day, and after the evening prayer. These are your three times of privacy. No blame shall attach to you or to them, if after these times, when ye go your rounds of attendance on one another, they come in without permission. Thus doth God make clear to you His signs: and God is Knowing, Wise

24:59.t: And when your children come of age, let them ask leave to come into your presence, as they who were before them asked it. Thus doth God make clear to you his signs: and God is Knowing, Wise

24:60.t: As to women who are past childbearing, and have no hope of marriage, no blame shall attach to them if they lay aside their outer garments, but so as not to shew their ornaments. Yet if they abstain from this, it will be better for them: and God Heareth, Knoweth

24:61.t: No crime shall it be in the blind, or in the lame, or in the sick, to eat at your tables: or in yourselves, if ye eat in your own houses, or in the houses of your fathers, or of your mothers, or of your brothers, or of your sisters, or of your uncles on the father's side, or of your aunts on the father's side, or of your uncles on the mother's side, or of your aunts on the mother's side, or in those of which ye possess the keys, or in the house of your friend. No blame shall attach to you whether ye eat together or apart. And when ye enter houses, salute one another with a good and blessed greeting as from God. Thus doth God make clear to you His signs, that haply ye may comprehend them

24:62.t: Verily, they only are believers who believe in God and His Apostle, and who, when they are with him upon any affair of common interest, depart not until they have sought his leave. Yes, they who ask leave of thee, are those who believe in God and His Apostle. And when they ask leave of Thee on account of any affairs of their own, then grant it to those of them whom thou wilt, and ask indulgence for them of God: for God is Indulgent, Merciful

24:63.t: Address not the Apostle as ye address one another. God knoweth those of you who withdraw quietly from the assemblies, screening themselves behind others. And let those who transgress his command beware, lest some present trouble befall them, or a grievous chastisement befall them, hereafter

24:64.t: Is not whatever is in the Heavens and the Earth God's? He knoweth your state; and one day shall men be assembled before Him, and He will tell them of what they have done: for God knoweth all things

25:1.t: BLESSED be He who hath sent down AL FURKAN
on his servant, that to all creatures he may be a warner

25:2.t: His the Kingdom of the Heavens and of the Earth! No son hath He begotten! No partner hath He in his Empire! All things hath He created, and decreeing hath decreed their destinies

25:3.t: Yet have they adopted gods beside Him which have created nothing, but were themselves created: And no power have they over themselves for evil or for good, nor have they power of death, or of life, or of raising the dead

25:4.t: And the infidels say, "This Koran is a mere fraud of his own devising, and others have helped him with it, who had come hither by outrage and lie

25:5.t: And they say, "Tales of the ancients that he hath put in writing! and they were dictated to him morn and even

25:6.t: SAY: He hath sent it down who knoweth the secrets of the Heavens and of the Earth. He truly is the Gracious, the Merciful

25:7.t: And they say, "What sort of apostle is this? He eateth food and he walketh the streets! Unless an angel be sent down and take part in his warnings

25:8.t: Or a treasure be thrown down to him, or he have a garden that supplieth him with food..." and those unjust persons say, "Ye follow but a man enchanted

25:9.t: See what likenesses they strike out for thee! But they err, and cannot find their way

25:10.t: Blessed be He who if he please can give thee better than that of which they speak - Gardens, 'neath which the rivers flow: and pavilions will He assign thee

25:11.t: Aye, they have treated the coming of "the Hour" as a lie. But a flaming fire have we got ready for those who treat the coming of the Hour as a lie

25:12.t: When it shall see them from afar, they shall hear its raging and roaring

25:13.t: And when they shall be flung into a narrow space thereof bound together, they shall invoke destruction on the spot

25:14.t: Call not this day for one destruction, but call for destructions many

25:15.t: SAY: Is this, or the Paradise of Eternity which was promised to the God-fearing, best? Their recompense shall it be and their retreat

25:16.t: Abiding therein for ever, they shall have in it all that they desire! It is a promise to be claimed of thy Lord

25:17.t: And on the day when he shall gather them together, and those whom they worshipped beside God, he will say, "Was it ye who led these my servants astray, or of themselves strayed they from the path

25:18.t: They will say, "Glory be to thee! It beseemed not us to take other lords than thee. But thou gavest them and their fathers their fill of good things, till they forgat the remembrance of thee, and became a lost people

25:19.t: Then will God say to the Idolaters, "Now have they made you liars in what ye say, and they have no power to avert your doom, or to succour you." whosoever of you thus offendeth, we will make him taste a great punishment

25:20.t: Never have we sent Apostles before thee who ate not common food, and walked not the streets. And we test you by means of each other. Will ye be steadfast? Thy Lord is looking on

25:21.t: They who look not forward to meet Us say, "If the angels be not sent down to us, or unless we behold our Lord...." Ah! they are proud of heart, and exceed with great excess

25:22.t: On the day when they shall see the angels, no good news shall there be for the guilty ones, and they shall cry out, "A barrier that cannot be passed

25:23.t: Then will we proceed to the works which they have wrought, and make them as scattered dust

25:24.t: Happier, on that day, the inmates of the Garden as to abode, and better off as to place of noontide slumber

25:25.t: On that day shall the heaven with its clouds be cleft, and the angels shall be sent down, descending

25:26.t: On that day shall all empire be in very deed with the God of Mercy, and a hard day shall it be for the Infidels

25:27.t: And on that day shall the wicked one bite his hands, and say, "Oh! would that I had taken the same path with the Apostle

25:28.t: Oh! woe is me! would that I had not taken such an one for my friend

25:29.t: It was he who led me astray from the Warning which had reached me! and Satan is man's betrayer

25:30.t: Then said the Apostle, "O my Lord! truly my people have esteemed this Koran to be vain babbling

25:31.t: Thus have we given to every Prophet an enemy from among the wicked ones - But thy Lord is a sufficient guide and helper

25:32.t: And the infidels say, "Unless the Koran be sent down to him all at once...." But in this way would we stablish thy heart by it; in parcels have we parcelled it out to thee

25:33.t: Nor shall they come to thee with puzzling questions, but we will come to thee with the truth, and their best solution

25:34.t: They who shall be gathered upon their faces into hell, shall have the worst place, and be farthest from the path of happiness

25:35.t: Heretofore we gave the law to Moses, and appointed his brother Aaron to be his counsellor

25:36.t: And we said, "Go ye to the people who treat our signs as lies." And them destroyed we with utter destruction

25:37.t: And as to the people of Noah! when they treated their Apostles as impostors, we drowned them; and we made them a sign to mankind: - A grievous chastisement have we prepared for the wicked

25:38.t: And Ad and Themoud, and the men of Rass, and divers generations between them

25:39.t: Unto each of them did we set forth parables for warnings, and each of them did we utterly exterminate

25:40.t: Oft are this have the unbelieving Meccans passed by the city on which was rained a fatal rain. What! Have they not seen it? Yet have they no hope of a resurrection

25:41.t: And when they see thee, they do but take thee as the subject of their railleries. "What! Is this he whom God has sent as an Apostle

25:42.t: Indeed he had well nigh led us astray from our gods, had we not persevered steadfastly in their service." But in the end they shall know, when they shall see the punishment, who hath most strayed from the path

25:43.t: What thinkest thou? He who hath taken his passions as a god - wilt thou be a guardian over him

25:44.t: Thinkest thou that the greater part of them hear or understand? They are just like the brutes! Yes! they stray even further from the right way

25:45.t: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord lengtheneth out the shadow? Had He pleased he had made it motionless. But we made the sun to be its guide

25:46.t: Then draw it in unto Us with easy indrawing

25:47.t: He it is who ordaineth the night as a garment, and sleep for rest, and ordaineth the day for waking up to life

25:48.t: He it is who sendeth the winds as the forerunner of his mercy
; and pure water send we down from Heaven

25:49.t: That we may revive by it a dead land: and we give it for drink to our creation, beasts and men in numbers

25:50.t: And we distribute it among them on all sides, that they may reflect: but most men refuse to be aught but thankless

25:51.t: Had we pleased, we had raised up a warner in every city

25:52.t: Give not way therefore to the Infidels, but by means of this Koran strive against them with a mighty strife

25:53.t: And He it is who hath let loose the two seas, the one sweet, fresh; and the other salt, bitter; and hath put an interspace between them, and a barrier that cannot be passed

25:54.t: And it is He who hath created man of water, and established between them the ties of kindred and affinity: and potent is thy Lord

25:55.t: Yet beside God do they worship what can neither help nor hurt them: and the Infidel is Satan's helper against his Lord

25:56.t: Still we have sent thee only as a herald and a warner

25:57.t: SAY: I ask of you no recompense for it, except from him who is willing to take the way to his Lord

25:58.t: And put thou thy trust in Him that liveth and dieth not, and celebrate his praise;
He fully knoweth the faults of his servants

25:59.t: who in six days created the Heavens and the Earth, and whatever is between them, then mounted his Throne: the God of Mercy! Ask now of the Wise concerning Him

25:60.t: But when it is said to them, "Bow down before the God of Mercy," they say, "Who is the God of Mercy? Shall we bow down to what thou biddest?" And they fly from thee the more

25:61.t: Blessed be He who hath placed in the Heaven the sign of the Zodiac! who hath placed in it the Lamp of the Sun, and the light-giving Moon

25:62.t: And it is He who hath ordained the night and the day to succeed one another for those who desire to think on God or desire to be thankful

25:63.t: And the servants of the God of Mercy are they who walk upon the Earth softly; and when the ignorant address them, they reply, "Peace

25:64.t: They that pass the night in the worship of their lord prostrate and standing

25:65.t: And that say, "O our Lord! turn away from us the torment of Hell, for its torment is endless

25:66.t: it is indeed an ill abode and resting place

25:67.t: Those who when they spend are neither lavish nor niggard, but keep the mean

25:68.t: Those who call on no other gods with God, nor slay whom God hath forbidden to be slain, except for a just cause, and who commit not fornication
for he who doth this shall meet the reward of his wickedness

25:69.t: Doubled to him shall be the torment on the day of Resurrection; and in it shall he remain, disgraced, for ever

25:70.t: Save those who shall repent and believe and do righteous works - for them God will change their evil things into good things, for God is Gracious, Merciful

25:71.t: And whose turneth to God and doeth what is right, he verily will convert with a true conversion

25:72.t: And they who bear not witness to that which is false, and when they pass by frivolous sport, pass on with dignity

25:73.t: And they who, when monished by the signs of their Lord, fall not down thereat, as if deaf and blind

25:74.t: And who say, "O our Lord! give us in our wives and offspring the joy of our eyes, and make us examples to those who fear thee

25:75.t: These shall be rewarded with the High Places of Paradise for their steadfast endurance, and they shall meet therein with - Welcome and Salutation

25:76.t: For ever shall they remain therein: a fair abode and resting-place

25:77.t: SAY: Not on your account doth my Lord care if ye call not on Him! ye have treated his Apostle as an impostor: but bye and bye a punishment shall cleave to them

26:2.t: These are the signs of the lucid Book

26:3.t: Haply thou wearest thyself away with grief because they will not believe

26:4.t: Were it our will we could send down to them a sign from Heaven, before which they would humbly bow

26:5.t: But from each fresh warning that cometh to them from the God of Mercy they have only turned aside

26:6.t: And treated it as a lie: But tidings shall reach them which they shall not laugh to scorn

26:7.t: Have they not beheld the earth - how we have caused every kind of noble plant to spring up therein

26:8.t: Verily, in this is a sign: but most of them believe not

26:9.t: And assuredly, thy Lord! - He is the Mighty, the Merciful

26:10.t: And remember when thy Lord called to Moses, "Go to the wicked people

26:11.t: The people of Pharaoh. What! will they not fear me

26:12.t: He said, "My Lord, in sooth I fear lest they treat me as a liar

26:13.t: And my breast is straitened, and I am slow of speech: send therefore to Aaron to be my helpmate

26:14.t: For they have a charge against me, and I fear lest they put me to death

26:15.t: He said, "Surely not. Go ye therefore with our signs: we will be with you and will hearken

26:16.t: And go to Pharaoh and say: 'Verily we are the messengers of the Lord of the worlds

26:17.t: Send forth with us the children of Israel

26:18.t: He said, "Did we not rear thee among us when a child? And hast thou not passed years of thy life among us

26:19.t: And yet what a deed is that which thou hast done! Thou art one of the ungrateful

26:20.t: He said, "I did it indeed, and I was one of those who erred

26:21.t: And I fled from you because I feared you; but my Lord hath given me wisdom and hath made me one of his Apostles

26:22.t: And is this the favour thou hast conferred on me, that thou hast enslaved the children of Israel

26:23.t: Said Pharaoh, "Who then is the Lord of the Worlds

26:24.t: He said, "The Lord of the Heavens and of the Earth and of all that is between them, if only ye believe it

26:25.t: Said Pharaoh to those around him, "Hear ye this

26:26.t: Your Lord," said Moses, "and the Lord of your sires of old

26:27.t: In sooth, your Apostle whom He hath sent to you," said Pharaoh, "is certainly possessed

26:28.t: He said, "Lord is He of the East and of the West, and of all that is between them, if ye can understand

26:29.t: He said, "If ye take any God beside me, I will surely put thee in ward

26:30.t: Said Moses, "What! if I shew thee that which shall be a proof of my mission

26:31.t: He said, "Forth with it then, if thou speakest truth

26:32.t: Then threw he down his staff, and lo! an undoubted serpent

26:33.t: And he drew out his hand, and lo! it was white to the beholders

26:34.t: He said to his nobles around him. "This truly is a right cunning sorcerer

26:35.t: Fain would he drive you out of your land by his Sorcery. But what do ye suggest

26:36.t: They said, "Put him and his brother off awhile, and send summoners to all the cities

26:37.t: Who shall bring to thee every cunning magician

26:38.t: So the magicians were mustered at a set time, on a solemn day

26:39.t: And it was said to the people, "Are ye all assembled

26:40.t: Yes! and we will follow the magicians if they gain the day

26:41.t: And when the magicians were arrived they said to Pharaoh, "Shall we have a reward if we gain the day

26:42.t: He said, "Yes. And verily in that case ye shall be of those who are near my person

26:43.t: Moses said to them, "Throw down what ye have to throw

26:44.t: So they cast down their ropes and rods, and said, "By Pharaoh's might we shall surely win

26:45.t: Then Moses threw down his rod, and lo! it swallowed up their cheating wonders

26:46.t: Then the magicians threw themselves down in worship

26:47.t: They said, "We believe on the Lord of the Worlds

26:48.t: The Lord of Moses and of Aaron

26:49.t: Said Pharaoh, "Have ye then believed on him ere I gave you leave? He truly is your master who hath taught you magic. But bye and bye ye shall surely know my power. I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will have you all crucified

26:50.t: They said, "It cannot harm us, for to our Lord shall we return

26:51.t: Assuredly we trust that our Lord will forgive us our sins, since we are of the first who believe

26:52.t: Then revealed we this order to Moses: "Go forth by night with my servants, for ye will be pursued

26:53.t: And Pharaoh sent summoners through the cities

26:54.t: These Israelites," said they, "are a scanty band

26:55.t: Yet are they enraged against us

26:56.t: But we truly are numerous, wary

26:57.t: Thus we caused them to quit gardens and fountains

26:59.t: So was it; and we gave them to the children of Israel for an heritage

26:60.t: Then at sunrise the Egyptians followed them

26:61.t: And when the hosts came in view of one another, the comrades of Moses said, "We are surely overtaken

26:62.t: He said, "By no means: - for my Lord is with me - He will guide me

26:63.t: And we revealed this order to Moses, "Strike the sea with thy rod." And it clave asunder, and each part became like a huge mountain

26:64.t: Then made we the others to draw on

26:65.t: And we saved Moses, and those who were with him, all

26:67.t: Truly in this was a sign; but most of them did not believe

26:68.t: But verily thy Lord, - He is the Mighty, the Merciful

26:69.t: And recite to them the story of Abraham

26:70.t: When he said to his Father and to his people, "What worship ye

26:71.t: They said, "We worship idols, and constant is our devotion to them

26:72.t: He said, "Can they hear you when ye cry to them

26:73.t: Or help you or do you harm

26:74.t: They said, "But we found our Fathers do the like

26:75.t: He said, "How think ye? They whom ye worship

26:76.t: Ye and your fathers of early days

26:77.t: Are my foes: but not so the Lord of the Worlds

26:78.t: Who hath created me, and guideth me

26:79.t: Who giveth me food and drink

26:80.t: And when I am sick, he healeth me

26:81.t: And who will cause me to die and again quicken me

26:82.t: And who, I hope, will forgive me my sins in the day of reckoning

26:83.t: My Lord! bestow on me wisdom and join me to the just

26:84.t: And give me a good name among posterity

26:85.t: And make me one of the heirs of the garden of delight

26:86.t: And forgive my father, for he was one of the erring

26:87.t: And put me not to shame on the day when mankind shall be raised up

26:88.t: The day when neither wealth nor children shall avail

26:89.t: Save to him who shall come to God with a sound heart

26:90.t: When Paradise shall be brought near the pious

26:91.t: And Hell shall lay open for those who have gone astray

26:92.t: And it shall be said to them, 'Where are they whom ye worshipped

26:93.t: Beside God? Can they harm you or help themselves

26:94.t: And they shall be cast into it - the seducers and the seduced

26:95.t: And all the host of Eblis

26:96.t: They shall say, as they wrangle therein together

26:97.t: By God, we were in a plain error

26:98.t: When we equalled you with the Lord of the Worlds

26:99.t: And none misled us but the wicked

26:100.t: And we have none to plead for us

26:101.t: Nor friend who careth for us

26:102.t: Could we but return, we would be of the believers

26:103.t: Verily, in this was a sign: but most of them believed not

26:104.t: And truly thy Lord! - He is the Mighty, the Merciful

26:105.t: The people of Noah gainsaid the Apostles

26:106.t: When their brother Noah said to them, "Will ye not fear God

26:107.t: Of a truth am I your faithful Apostle

26:108.t: Fear God then and obey me

26:109.t: I ask of you no reward for this, for my reward is of the Lord of the Worlds alone

26:110.t: Fear God then and obey me

26:111.t: They said, "Shall we believe on thee when the meanest only are thy followers

26:112.t: He said, "But I have no knowledge of that they did

26:113.t: To my Lord only must their account be given: would that ye understood this

26:114.t: And I will not thrust away those who believe

26:115.t: For I am only one charged with plain warnings

26:116.t: They said, "Now unless thou desist, O Noah, one of the stoned shalt thou surely be

26:117.t: He said, "Lord! my people treat me as a liar

26:118.t: Decide thou therefore a decision between me and them, and rescue me and the faithful who are with me

26:119.t: So we saved him and those who were with him in the fully-laden ark

26:120.t: And afterwards we drowned the rest

26:121.t: Herein truly was a sign, but most of them believed not

26:122.t: But thy Lord! - He is the Mighty, the Merciful

26:123.t: The Adites treated their Apostles as liars

26:124.t: When their brother Houd said to them, "Will ye not fear God

26:125.t: I am your Apostle, worthy of all credit

26:126.t: Fear God then and obey me

26:127.t: I ask for no reward for this; for my reward is of the Lord of the Worlds alone

26:128.t: What! build ye landmarks on all heights in mere pastime

26:129.t: And raise ye structures to be your lasting abodes

26:130.t: And when ye put forth your power do ye put it forth with harshness

26:131.t: Fear ye God then and obey me

26:132.t: And fear ye Him who hath plenteously betowed on you ye well know what

26:133.t: Plenteously bestowed on you flocks and children

26:135.t: Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day

26:136.t: They said, "It is the same to us whether thou warn or warn us not

26:137.t: This is but a tale of the ancients

26:138.t: And we are not they who shall be punished

26:139.t: And they charged him with imposture; and we destroyed them. In this was a sign: but most of them believed not

26:140.t: But thy Lord! - He is the Mighty, the Merciful

26:141.t: The Themoudites also treated their Apostles as liars

26:142.t: When their brother Saleh said to them, "Will ye not fear God

26:143.t: I am your Apostle worthy of all credit

26:144.t: Fear God, then, and obey me

26:145.t: I ask of you no reward for this: my reward is of the Lord of the Worlds alone

26:146.t: Shall ye be left secure amid these things here

26:148.t: And corn-fields and palm-trees, with flower-sheathing branches

26:149.t: And, insolent that ye are, will ye hew out your dwellings in the mountains

26:150.t: But fear God and obey me

26:151.t: And obey not the bidding of those who commit excess

26:152.t: Who act disorderly on the earth and reform it not

26:153.t: They said, "Certainly thou art a person bewitched

26:154.t: Thou art only a man like us: produce now a sign if thou art a man of truth

26:155.t: He said, "This she-camel, then - drink shall there be for her, and drink shall there be for you, on a several day for each

26:156.t: But harm her not, lest the punishment of a tremendous day overtake you

26:157.t: But they ham-strung her, and repented of it on the morrow

26:158.t: For the punishment overtook them. In this truly was a sign, but most of them believed not

26:159.t: But thy Lord! - He is the Powerful, the Merciful

26:160.t: The people of Lot treated their apostles as liars

26:161.t: When their brother Lot said to them, "Will ye not fear God

26:162.t: I am your Apostle worthy of all credit

26:163.t: Fear God, then, and obey me

26:164.t: For this I ask you no reward: my reward is of the Lord of the worlds alone

26:165.t: What! with men, of all creatures, will ye have commerce

26:166.t: And leave ye your wives whom your Lord hath created for you? Ah! ye are an erring people

26:167.t: They said, "O Lot, if thou desist not, one of the banished shalt thou surely be

26:168.t: He said, "I utterly abhor your doings

26:169.t: My Lord! deliver me and my family from what they do

26:170.t: So we delivered him and his whole family

26:171.t: Save an aged one among those who tarried

26:173.t: And we rained a rain upon them, and fatal was the rain to those whom we had warned

26:174.t: In this truly was a sign; but most of them did not believe

26:175.t: But thy Lord! He is the Powerful, the Merciful

26:176.t: The dwellers in the forest of Madian treated the Apostles as liars

26:177.t: When Shoaib their brother said to them, "Will ye not fear God

26:178.t: I truly am your trustworthy Apostle

26:179.t: Fear God, then, and obey me

26:180.t: No reward ask I of you for this: my reward is of the Lord of the Worlds alone

26:181.t: Fill the measure, and be not of those who minish

26:183.t: And defraud not men in their substance, and do no wrong on the earth by deeds of licence

26:184.t: And fear Him who made you and the races of old

26:185.t: They said, "Certainly thou art a person bewitched

26:186.t: Thou art but a man like us, and we deem thee liar

26:187.t: Make now a part of the heaven to fall down upon us, if thou art a man of truth

26:188.t: He said, "My Lord best knoweth your doings

26:189.t: And when they treated him as a liar, the chastisement of the day of cloud overtook them. This truly was the chastisement of a dreadful day

26:190.t: In this was a sign, but most of them believed not

26:191.t: But thy Lord! - He is the Mighty, the Merciful

26:192.t: Verily from the Lord of the Worlds hath this Book come down

26:193.t: The faithful spirit hath come down with it

26:194.t: Upon thy heart, that thou mightest become a warner

26:196.t: And truly it is foretold in the Scriptures of them of yore

26:197.t: Was it not a sign to them that the learned among the children of Israel recognised it

26:198.t: If we had sent it down unto any foreigner

26:199.t: And he had recited it to them, they had not believed

26:200.t: In such sort have we influenced the heart of the wicked ones

26:201.t: That they will not believe it till they see the grievous chastisement

26:202.t: And it shall come upon them on a sudden when they look not for it

26:203.t: And they will say, "Can we be respited

26:204.t: What! will they seek to hasten on our chastisement

26:205.t: How thinkest thou? If after we have given them their fill for years

26:206.t: That with which they are menaced come upon them at last

26:207.t: Of what avail will their enjoyments be to them

26:208.t: We never destroyed a city which had not first its warners

26:209.t: With admonition; nor did we deal unjustly

26:210.t: The Satans were not sent down with this Koran

26:211.t: It beseemed them not, and they had not the power

26:212.t: For they are far removed from hearing it

26:213.t: Call not thou on any other god but God, lest thou be of those consigned to torment

26:214.t: But warn thy relatives of nearer kin

26:215.t: And kindly lower thy wing over the faithful who follow thee

26:216.t: And if they disobey thee, then say: "I will not be answerable for your doings

26:217.t: And put thy trust in Him that is the Mighty, the Merciful

26:218.t: Who seeth thee when thou standest in prayer

26:219.t: And thy demeanour amongst those who worship

26:221.t: Shall I tell you on whom Satan descend

26:222.t: They descend on every lying, wicked person

26:223.t: They impart what they have heard; - but most of them are liars

26:224.t: It is the POETS whom the erring follow

26:225.t: Seest thou not how they rove distraught in every valley

26:226.t: And that they say that which they do not

26:227.t: Save those who believe and do good works, and oft remember God; And who defend themselves when unjustly treated. But they who treat them unjustly shall find out what a lot awaiteth them

27:1.t: TA. SAD. These are the signs
of the Koran and of the lucid Book

27:2.t: Guidance and glad tidings to the believers

27:3.t: who observe prayer and pay the stated alms, and believe firmly - do they - in the life to come

27:4.t: As to those who believe not in the life to come, we have made their own doings fair seeming to them, and they are bewildered therein

27:5.t: These are they whom the woe of chastisement awaiteth; and in the next life they shall suffer - yes shall they - greatest loss

27:6.t: But thou hast certainly received the Koran from the Wise, the Knowing

27:7.t: Bear in mind when Moses said to his family, "I have perceived a fire; I will bring you tidings from it, or will bring you a blazing brand, that ye may warm you

27:8.t: And when he came to it, he was called to, "Blessed, He who is in the fire, and He who is about it; and glory be to God, the Lord of the worlds

27:9.t: O Moses! verily, I am God, the Mighty, the Wise

27:10.t: Throw down now thy staff." And when he saw that it moved itself as though it were a serpent, he retreated backward and returned not. "O Moses, fear not; for the Sent Ones fear not in my presence

27:11.t: Save he who having done amiss shall afterwards exchange the evil for good; for I am Forgiving, Merciful

27:12.t: Put now thy hand into thy bosom: it shall come forth white, yet free from hurt: one of nine signs to Pharaoh and his people; for a perverse people are they

27:13.t: And when our signs were wrought in their very sight, they said, "This is plain magic

27:14.t: And though in their souls they knew them to be true, yet in their wickedness and pride they denied them. But see what was the end of the corrupt doers

27:15.t: And of old we gave knowledge to David and Solomon: and they said, "Praise be to God, who hath made us to excel many of his believing servants

27:16.t: And in knowledge Solomon was David's heir. And he said, "O men, we have been taught the speech of birds, and are endued with everything. This is indeed a clear boon from God

27:17.t: And to Solomon were gathered his hosts of Djinn and men and birds, and they were marched on in bands

27:18.t: Till they reached the Valley of Ants. Said AN ANT, "O ye ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his army crush you and know it not

27:19.t: Then smiled Solomon, laughing at her words, and he said, "Stir me up, O Lord, to be thankful for thy favour which thou hast shewed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that shall be well pleasing to thee, and bring me in, by thy mercy, among thy servants the righteous

27:20.t: And he reviewed the birds, and said, "How is it that I see not the lapwing? Is it one of the absent

27:21.t: Surely, with a severe chastisement will I chastise it, or I will certainly slaughter it, unless it bring me a clear excuse

27:22.t: Nor tarried it long ere it came and said, "I have gained the knowledge that thou knowest not, and with sure tidings have I come to thee from Saba

27:23.t: I found a woman reigning over them, gifted with everything, and she hath a splendid throne

27:24.t: And I found her and her people worshipping the sun instead of God; and Satan hath made their works fair seeming to them, so that he hath turned them from the Way: wherefore they are not guided

27:25.t: To the worship of God, who bringeth to light the secret things of heaven and earth, and knoweth what men conceal and what they manifest

27:26.t: God! there is no god but He! the lord of the glorious throne

27:27.t: He said, "We shall see whether thou hast spoken truth, or whether thou art of them that lie

27:28.t: Go with this my letter and throw it down to them: then turn away from them and await their answer

27:29.t: She said, "O my nobles! an honourable letter hath been thrown down to me

27:30.t: It is from Solomon; and it is this: 'In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

27:31.t: Set not up yourselves against me, but come to me submitting

27:32.t: She said, "O my nobles, advise me in mine affair: I decide it not without your concurrence

27:33.t: They said, "We are endued with strength and are endued with mighty valour. - But to command is thine: See therefore what thou wilt command us

27:34.t: She said, "Kings when they enter a city spoil it, and abase the mightiest of its people: and in like manner will these also do

27:35.t: But I will send to them with a gift, and await what my envoys bring back

27:36.t: And when the messenger came to Solomon, he said, "Aid ye me with riches? But what God hath given to me is better than what he hath given you: yet ye glory in your gifts

27:37.t: Return to them: for we will surely come to them with forces which they cannot withstand, and we will drive them from their land humbled and contemptible

27:38.t: Said he, "O nobles, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me, submitting?

27:39.t: An Efreet of the Djinn said: "I will bring it thee ere thou risest from thy place: I have power for this and am trusty

27:40.t: And one who had the knowledge of Scripture said, "I will bring it to thee in the twinkling of an eye." And when he saw it set before him, he said, "This is of the favour of my Lord, to try me whether I will be thankful or unthankful. And he who is thankful is thankful to his own behoof; and as for him who is unthankful - truly my Lord is self-sufficient, bounteous

27:41.t: Said he, "Make her throne so that she know it not: we shall see whether she hath or not guidance

27:42.t: And when she came he said, "Is thy throne like this?" She said, "As though it were the same." "And we," said he, "have had knowledge given us before her, and have been Muslims

27:43.t: But the gods she had worshipped instead of God had led her astray: for she was of a people who believe not

27:44.t: It was said to her,"Enter the Palace:" and when she saw it, she thought it a lake of water, and bared her legs. He said, "It is a palace paved with glass." She said, "O my Lord! I have sinned against my own soul, and I resign myself, with Solomon, to God the Lord of the Worlds

27:45.t: And of old we sent to Themoud their brother Saleh, with "Serve ye God:"but lo! they became two sets of disputants wrangling with each other

27:46.t: He said, "O my people, why, if ye ask not pardon of God that ye may find mercy, hasten ye on evil rather than good

27:47.t: They said,"We augur ill concerning thee and those who are with thee." He said, "The ills of which ye augur depend on God. But ye are a people on your trial

27:48.t: And there were in the city nine persons who committed excesses in the land and did not that which is right

27:49.t: They said, "Swear ye to one another by God that we will surely fall on him and on his family by night: then will be say to the avenger of blood, we witnessed not the destruction of his family: and verily we speak the truth

27:50.t: And they devised a device, and we devised a device, and they were not aware of it

27:51.t: And see what was the end of their device! We destroyed them and their whole people

27:52.t: And for their sin these their houses are empty ruins: Verily in this is a sign to those who understand

27:53.t: And we delivered those who believed and feared

27:54.t: And Lot, when he said to his people, "What! proceed ye to such filthiness with your eyes open

27:55.t: What! come ye with lust unto men rather than to women? Surely ye are an ignorant people

27:56.t: And the answer of his people was but to say, "Cast out the family of Lot from your city: they, forsooth, are men of purity

27:57.t: So we rescued him and his family: but as for his wife, we decreed her to be of them that lingered

27:58.t: And we rained a rain upon them, and fatal was the rain to those who had had their warning

27:59.t: SAY: Praise be to God and peace be on His servants whom He hath chosen! Is God the more worthy or the gods they join with Him

27:60.t: Is not He who hath made the Heavens and the Earth, and hath sent down rain to you from Heaven, by which we cause the luxuriant groves to spring up! It is not in your power to cause its trees to spring up! What! A god with God? Yet they find equals for Him

27:61.t: Is not He, who hath set the earth so firm, and hath made rivers in its midst, and hath placed mountains upon it, and put a barrier between the two seas? What! a god with God? Yet the greater part of them have no knowledge

27:62.t: Is not He the more worthy who answereth the oppressed when they cry to him, and taketh off their ills, and maketh you to succeed your sires on the earth? What! a god with God? How few bear these things in mind

27:63.t: Is not He, who guideth you in the darkness of the land and of the sea, and who sendeth forth the winds as the forerunners of His mercy? What! a god with God? Far from God be what ye join with Him

27:64.t: Is not He, who created a Being, then reneweth it, and who supplieth you out of the Heaven and the Earth? What! a god with God? SAY: Bring forth your proofs if you speak the truth

27:65.t: SAY: None either in the Heavens or in the Earth knoweth the unseen but God. And they know not When they shall be raised

27:66.t: Yet they have attained to a knowledge of the life to come: - yet are they in doubt about it: - yet are they blind about it

27:67.t: And the unbelievers say: "When we and our fathers have been dead shall we be taken forth

27:68.t: Of old have we been promised this, we and our sires of old it is but fables of the ancients

27:69.t: SAY: Go ye through the land, and see what hath been the end of the wicked

27:70.t: And grieve not thou for them, nor be in distress at their devisings

27:71.t: And they say, "When will this promise be made good, if ye speak true

27:72.t: SAY: Haply a part of what ye desire to be hastened may be close behind you

27:73.t: And truly thy Lord is full of goodness towards men: But most of them are not thankful

27:74.t: And thy Lord knoweth well what their breasts enshroud, and what they bring to light

27:75.t: And there is no secret thing in the Heaven or on the Earth, but it is in the clear Book

27:76.t: Truly this Koran declareth to the children of Israel most things wherein they disagree

27:77.t: And it is certainly guidance and a mercy to the faithful

27:78.t: Verily, by his wisdom will thy Lord decide between them: for He is the Mighty, the Knowing

27:79.t: Put thou then thy trust in God: for thou hast clear truth on thy side

27:80.t: Thou shalt not make the dead to hear; neither shalt thou make the deaf to hear the call, when they turn away backward

27:81.t: Neither art thou the guide of the blind out of their errors: none truly shalt thou make to hear but those who believe our signs: and they are Muslims

27:82.t: When the doom shall be ready to light upon them, we will cause a monster to come forth to them out of the earth, and cry to them "Verily men have not firmly believed our signs

27:83.t: And on that day shall be gathered out of every nation a company of those who have gainsaid our signs, in separate bands

27:84.t: Till they come before God, who will say, "Treated ye my signs as impostures, although ye embraced them not in your knowledge? or what is it that ye were doing

27:85.t: And doom shall light upon them for their evil deeds, and nought shall they have to plead

27:86.t: See they not that we have ordained the night that they may rest in it, and the day with its gift of light? Of a truth herein are signs to people who believe

27:87.t: On that day there shall be a blast on the trumpet, and all that are in the heavens, and all that the on the earth shall be terror-stricken, save him whom God pleaseth to deliver; and all shall come to him in humble guise

27:88.t: And thou shalt see the mountains, which thou thinkest so firm, pass away with the passing of a cloud! 'Tis the work of God, who ordereth all things! of all that ye do is He well aware

27:89.t: To him who shall present himself with good works, shall be a reward beyond their desert, and they shall be secure from the terror on that day

27:90.t: And they who shall present themselves with evil shall be flung downward on their faces into the fire. Shall ye be rewarded but as ye have wrought

27:91.t: SAY: Specially am I commanded to worship the Lord of this land, which He hath sanctified. All things are His: and I am commanded to be one of those who surrender them to God

27:92.t: And to recite the Koran: and whoever is rightly guided, assuredly will be rightly guided to his own behoof

27:93.t: And as to him who erreth, SAY, I truly am a warner only.And SAY, Praise be to God! He will shew you His signs, and ye shall acknowledge them: and of what ye do, thy Lord is not regardless

28:2.t: These are the signs of the lucid Book

28:3.t: We will recite to thee portions of the History of Moses and Pharaoh with truth, for the teaching of the faithful

28:4.t: Now Pharaoh lifted himself up in the earth, and divided his people into parties: one portion of them he brought low - He slew their male children, and let their females only live; for he was one of those who wrought disorders

28:5.t: And we were minded to shew favour to those who were brought low in the land, and to make them spiritual chiefs, and to make them Pharaoh's heirs

28:6.t: And to stablish them in the land; and to make Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts, the eye-witnesses of what they dreaded from them

28:7.t: And we said by revelation to the mother of Moses, "Give him suck; and if thou fearest for him, launch him on the sea; and fear not, neither fret; for we will restore him to thee, and make him one of the apostles

28:8.t: And Pharaoh's family took him up to be a foe and a sorrow to them, for sinners were Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts

28:9.t: And Pharaoh's wife said, "Joy of the eye to me and thee! put him not to death: haply he will be useful to us, or we may adopt him as a son." But they knew not what they did

28:10.t: And the heart of Moses' mother became a blank through fear: and almost had she discovered him, but that we girt up her heart with constancy, in order that she might be one of those who believe

28:11.t: She said to his sister, "Follow him." And she watched him from afar: and they perceived it not

28:12.t: And we caused him to refuse the nurses, until his sister came and said, Shall I point out to you the family of a house that will rear him for you, and will be careful of him

28:13.t: So we restored him to his mother, to be the joy of her eyes, and that she might not fret, and that she might know that the promise of God was true. But most men knew it not

28:14.t: And when he had reached his age of strength, and had become a man, we bestowed on him wisdom and knowledge; for thus do we reward the righteous

28:15.t: And he entered a city at the time when its inhabitants would not observe him, and found therein two men fighting: the one, of his own people; the other, of his enemies. And he who was of his own people asked his help against him who was of his enemies. And Moses smote him with his fist and slew him. Said he, "This is a work of Satan; for he is an enemy, a manifest misleader

28:16.t: He said, "O my Lord, I have sinned to mine own hurt: forgive me." So God forgave him; for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful

28:17.t: He said, "Lord, because thou hast showed me this grace, I will never again be the helper of the wicked

28:18.t: And in the city at noon he was full of fear, casting furtive glances round him: and lo! the man whom he had helped the day before, cried out to him again for help. Said Moses to him, "Thou art plainly a most depraved person

28:19.t: And when he would have laid violent hands on him who was their common foe, he said to him, "O Moses, dost thou desire to slay me, as thou slayedst a man yesterday? Thou desirest only to become a tyrant in this land, and desirest not to become a peacemaker

28:20.t: But a man came running up from the city's end. He said, "O Moses, of a truth, the nobles consult to slay thee - Begone then - I counsel thee as a friend

28:21.t: So forth he went from it in fear, looking warily about him. He said, "O Lord, deliver me from the unjust people

28:22.t: And when he was journeying toward Madian, he said, "Haply my Lord will direct me in an even path

28:23.t: And when he arrived at the water of Madian, he found at it a company of men watering. And he found beside them, two women keeping back their flock: "Why do ye," said he, "thus?" They said "We shall not water till the shepherds shall have driven off; for our father is very aged

28:24.t: So he watered for them - then retired to the shade and said, "O my Lord, of the good thou hast caused me to meet with I stand in need

28:25.t: And one of them came to him, walking bashfully. Said she, "My father calleth thee, that he may pay thee wages for thy watering for us." And when he came to him and had told him his STORY, "Fear not," said he, "thou hast escaped from an unjust people

28:26.t: One of them said, "O my father, hire him: for the best thou canst hire is the strong, the trusty

28:27.t: He said, "Truly to one of these my two daughters I desire to marry thee, if for eight years thou wilt be my hired servant: and if thou fulfil ten, it shall be of thine own accord, for I wish not to deal hardly with thee. Thou wilt find me, if God will, one of the upright

28:28.t: He said, "Be it so between me and thee: Whichever of the two terms I fulfil, there will be no injustice to me. And God is witness of what we say

28:29.t: And when Moses had fulfilled the term, and was journeying with his family, he perceived a fire on the mountain side. He said to his family, "Wait ye, for I perceive a fire. Haply I may bring you tidings from it, or a brand from the fire to warm you

28:30.t: And when he came up to it, a Voice cried to him out of the bush from the right side of the valley in the sacred hollow, "O Moses, I truly am God, the Lord of the Worlds

28:31.t: Throw down now thy rod." And when he saw it move as though it were a serpent, he retreated and fled and returned not. "O Moses," cried the Voice, "draw near and fear not, for thou art in safety

28:32.t: Put thy hand into thy bosom; it shall come forth white, but unharmed: and draw back thy hand to thee without fear. These shall be two signs from thy Lord to Pharaoh and his nobles; for they are a perverse people

28:33.t: He said, "O my Lord! truly I have slain one of them, therefore fear I lest they slay me

28:34.t: My brother Aaron is clearer of speech than I. Send him, therefore, with me as a help, and to make good my cause, for I fear lest they treat me as an impostor

28:35.t: He said, "We will strengthen thine arm with thy brother, and we will give power unto you both, and they shall not equal you in our signs. Ye twain and they who shall follow you, shall gain the day

28:36.t: And when Moses came to him with our demonstrative signs they said, "This is nought but magical device. We never heard the like among our sires of old

28:37.t: And Moses said, "My Lord best knoweth on whom He hath bestowed His guidance, and whose shall be the recompense of the abode of Paradise. Verily, the wicked shall not prosper

28:38.t: And Pharaoh said, "O ye nobles, ye have no other God that I know of but myself. Burn me then, Haman, bricks of clay, and build me a tower that I may mount up to the God of Moses, for in sooth, I deem him a liar

28:39.t: And he and his hosts behaved themselves proudly and unjustly on the earth, and thought that they should never be brought back to us

28:40.t: But we seized on him and his hosts and cast them into the sea: Behold, then, the end of the wrongful doers

28:41.t: And we made them imams who invite to the fire of hell, and on the day of Resurrection they shall not be helped

28:42.t: We followed them with a curse in this world, and covered shall they be with shame on the day of Resurrection

28:43.t: And after we had destroyed the former generations, we gave the book of the Law to Moses for man's enlightening, and a guidance and a mercy, that haply they might reflect

28:44.t: And thou wast not on the western slope of Sinai when we laid his charge on Moses, nor wast thou one of the witnesses

28:45.t: But we raised up generations after Moses, men whose days were lengthened; neither didst thou dwell among the inhabitants of Madian to rehearse to them our signs, but we sent Apostles to them

28:46.t: Nor wast thou on the slope of Sinai when we called to Moses, but it is of the mercy of thy Lord that thou warnest a people, to whom no warner had come before thee, to the intent that they should reflect

28:47.t: And that they should not say when a calamity shall befal them for their previous handy work, "O our Lord! why hast thou not sent an Apostle to us? Then we should have followed thy signs and have been of the believers

28:48.t: Yet when the truth came to them from our very presence, they said, "Unless the like powers be given to him that were given to Moses...." But did they not disbelieve in what of old was given to Moses? They said, "Two works of sorcery have helped each other;" and they said, "We disbelieve them both

28:49.t: SAY: Bring then a Book from before God which shall be a better guide than these, that I may follow it; if ye speak the truth

28:50.t: And if they answer thee not, then know that verily they are following their own caprices: and who goeth more widely astray than he who followeth his own caprice without guidance from God? for God guideth not the wicked

28:51.t: And now have we caused our word to come unto them, that they may be warned

28:52.t: They to whom we gave the Scriptures before IT, do in IT believe

28:53.t: And when it is recited to them they say, "We believe in it, for it is the truth from our Lord. We were Muslims before it came

28:54.t: Twice shall their reward be given them, for that they suffered with patience, and repelled evil with good, and gave alms out of that with which we provided them

28:55.t: And when they hear light discourse they withdraw from it, and say, "Our works for us and your works for you! Peace be on you! We are not in quest of fools

28:56.t: Thou truly canst not guide whom thou desirest; but God guideth whom He will; and He best knoweth those who yield to guidance

28:57.t: But they say, "If we follow the way in which thou art guided, we shall be driven from our country." But have we not established for them a sacred secure precinct, to which fruits of every kind, our gift for their support, are gathered together? But most of them have no knowledge

28:58.t: And how many cities have we destroyed that flourished in wanton ease! And these their dwellings have not been inhabited since their time save by a few, and it is we who became their heirs

28:59.t: But thy Lord did not destroy the cities till He had sent an apostle to their mother-city to rehearse our signs to its people: nor did we destroy the cities unless its people were unjust

28:60.t: And all that hath been bestowed on you is merely for enjoyment and pomp of this life present: but that which is with God is better and more lasting. Will ye not be wise

28:61.t: Shall he then to whom we have promised a goodly promise and who obtaineth it, be as he on whom we have bestowed the enjoyments of this life present, and who on the day of Resurrection shall be brought up for punishment

28:62.t: On that day will God cry to them and say, "Where are my companions, as ye supposed them

28:63.t: They on whom doom shall be justly pronounced will say, "O our Lord! these are they whom we led astray: we led them astray even as we had been led astray ourselves: Thou hast no cause of blame against us: It was not we whom they worshipped
