28:64.t: And it shall be said, "Call now on those whom ye made God's companions:" and they shall call on them, but they will not answer them. And they shall see the punishment, and wish that they had been guided aright

28:65.t: And on that day shall God call to them and say, "How answered ye the apostles

28:66.t: But on that day they shall be too blinded with confusion to give an account, nor shall they ask it of one another

28:67.t: Yet as to him who shall turn to God and believe and do the thing that is right, it may come to pass that he shall be among the happy

28:68.t: And thy Lord createth what he will and hath a free choice. But they, the false gods, have no power to choose. Glory be to God! and high let him be exalted above those whom they associate with him

28:69.t: And thy Lord knoweth what their breasts conceal and what they bring to light

28:70.t: And He is God! There is no god but He! His, all praise in this life and in the next, and His the power supreme, and to Him shall ye be brought back

28:71.t: SAY: What think ye? If God should enshroud you with a long night until the day of resurrection, what god beside God would bring you light? Will ye not then hearken

28:72.t: SAY: What think ye? If God should make it one long day for you until the day of resurrection, what god but God could bring you the night in which to take your rest? Will ye not then see

28:73.t: Of His mercy he hath made for you the night that ye may take your rest in it; and the day that ye may seek what ye need out of his bounteous supplies, and that ye may give thanks

28:74.t: One day God will call to them and say, "Where are my companions as ye supposed them

28:75.t: And we will bring up a witness out of every nation and say, "Bring your proofs." And they shall know that the truth is with God alone, and the gods of their own devising shall desert them

28:76.t: Now Korah was of the people of Moses: but he behaved haughtily toward them; for we had given him such treasure that its keys would have burdened a company of men of strength. When his people said to him, "Exult not, for God loveth not those who exult

28:77.t: But seek, by means of what God hath given thee, to attain the future Mansion; and neglect not thy part in this world, but be bounteous to others as God hath been bounteous to thee, and seek not to commit excesses on the earth; for God loveth not those who commit excesses

28:78.t: He said, "It hath been given me only on account of the knowledge that is in me." Did he not know that God had destroyed before him generations that were mightier than he in strength and had amassed more abundant wealth? But the wicked shall not be asked of their crimes

28:79.t: And Korah went forth to his people in his pomp. Those who were greedy for this present life said, "Oh that we had the like of that which hath been bestowed on Korah! Truly he is possessed of great good fortune

28:80.t: But they to whom knowledge had been given said, "Woe to you! the reward of God is better for him who believeth and worketh righteousness, and none shall win it but those who have patiently endured

28:81.t: And we clave the earth for him and for his palace, and he had no forces, in the place of God, to help him, nor was he among those who are succoured

28:82.t: And in the morning those who the day before had coveted his lot said, "Aha! God enlargeth supplies to whom he pleaseth of his servants, or is sparing. Had not God been gracious to us, He had caused it to cleave for us. Aha! the ungrateful can never prosper

28:83.t: As to this future mansion, we will bestow it on those who seek not to exalt them in the earth or to do wrong: And there is a happy issue for the God-fearing

28:84.t: Whoso doeth good shall have reward beyond its merits, and whoso doeth evil, they who do evil shall be rewarded only as they shall have wrought

28:85.t: He who hath sanctioned the Koran to thee will certainly bring thee to thy home. SAY: My Lord best knoweth who hath guidance, and who is in undoubted error

28:86.t: Thou didst never expect that the Book would be given thee. Of thy Lord's mercy only hath it been sent down. Be not thou helpful then to the unbelievers

28:87.t: Neither let them turn thee aside from the signs of God after they have been sent down to thee, but bid men to thy Lord; and be not among those who add gods to God

28:88.t: And call not on any other god with God. There is no god but He! Everything shall perish except Himself! Judgment is His, and to Him shall ye return

29:2.t: Think men that when they say, "We believe," they shall be let alone and not be put to proof

29:3.t: We put to proof those who lived before them; for God will surely take knowledge of those who are sincere, and will surely take knowledge of the liars

29:4.t: Think they who work evil that they shall escape Us? Ill do they judge

29:5.t: To him who hopeth to meet God, the set time of God will surely come. The Hearer, the Knower, He

29:6.t: Whoso maketh efforts for the faith, maketh them for his own good only. Verily God is rich enough to dispense with all creatures

29:7.t: And as to those who shall have believed and done the things that are right, their evil deeds will we surely blot out from them, and according to their best actions will we surely reward them

29:8.t: Moreover we have enjoined on man to shew kindness to parents: but if they strive with thee that thou join that with Me of which thou hast no knowledge, obey them not. To me do ye return, and then will I tell you of your doings

29:9.t: And those who shall have believed and done the things that are right, we will surely give them an entering in among the just

29:10.t: But some men say, "We believe in God," yet when they meet with sufferings in the cause of God, they regard trouble from man as chastisement from God. Yet if a success come from thy Lord they are sure to say, "We were on your side!" Doth not God well know what is in the breasts of his creatures

29:11.t: Yes, and God well knoweth those who believe, and He well knoweth the Hypocrites

29:12.t: The unbelievers say to the faithful, "Follow ye our way, and we will surely bear your sins." But not aught of their sins will they bear - verily they are liars

29:13.t: But their own burdens, and burdens beside their own burdens shall they surely bear: and inquisition shall be made of them on the day of Resurrection as to their false devices

29:14.t: Of old sent we Noah to his people: a thousand years save fifty did he tarry among them; and the flood overtook them in their wrongful doings

29:15.t: But we rescued him and those who were in the vessel; and we made it a sign to all men

29:16.t: And Abraham; when he said to his people, "Worship God and fear Him. This will be best for you, if ye have knowledge

29:17.t: Ye only worship idols beside God, and are the authors of a lie. Those whom ye worship beside God can give you no supplies: seek, then, your supplies from God; and serve Him and give Him thanks. To Him shall ye return

29:18.t: Suppose that ye treat me as a liar! nations before you have treated God's messenger as a liar; but open preaching is his only duty

29:19.t: See they not how God bringeth forth creation? and then causeth it to return again? This truly is easy for God

29:20.t: SAY, Go through the earth, and see how he hath brought forth created beings. Hereafter, with a second birth will God cause them to be born again; for God is Almighty

29:21.t: Whom He pleaseth will He chastise, and on whom He pleaseth will He have mercy, and to Him shall ye be taken back

29:22.t: And ye shall not invalidate his power either in the Earth or in the Heaven: and, save God, ye shall have neither patron nor helper

29:23.t: As for those who believe not in the signs of God, or that they shall ever meet him, these of my mercy shall despair, and these doth a grievous chastisement await

29:24.t: And the only answer of his people was to say, "Slay him or burn him." But from the fire did God save him! Verily, herein are signs to those who believe

29:25.t: And Abraham said, "Of a truth ye have taken idols along with God as your bond of union in this life present; But on the day of resurrection some of you shall deny the others, and some of you shall curse the others; and your abode shall be the fire, and ye shall have none to help

29:26.t: But Lot believed on him, and said, "I betake me to my Lord, for He truly is the Mighty, the Wise

29:27.t: And we bestowed on him Isaac and Jacob, and placed the gift of prophecy and the Scripture among his posterity; And we gave him his reward in this world, and in the next he shall be among the just

29:28.t: We sent also Lot: when he said to his people, "Proceed ye to a filthiness in which no people in the world hath ever gone before you

29:29.t: Proceed ye even to men? attack ye them on the highway? and proceed ye to the crime in your assemblies?" But the only answer of his people was to say, "Bring God's chastisement upon us, if thou art a man of truth

29:30.t: He cried: My Lord! help me against this polluted people

29:31.t: And when our messengers came to Abraham with the tidings of a son, they said, "Of a truth we will destroy the in-dwellers in this city, for its in-dwellers are evil doers

29:32.t: He said, "Lot is therein." They said, "We know full well who therein is. Him and his family will we save, except his wife; she will be of those who linger

29:33.t: And when our messengers came to Lot, he was troubled for them, and his arm was too weak to protect them; and they said, "Fear not, and distress not thyself, for thee and thy family will we save, except thy wife; she will be of those who linger

29:34.t: We will surely bring down upon the dwellers in this city vengeance from Heaven for the excesses they have committed

29:35.t: And in what we have left of it is a clear sign to men of understanding

29:36.t: And to Madian we sent their brother Shoaib. And he said, "Oh! my people! worship God, and expect the latter day, and enact not in the land deeds of harmful excess

29:37.t: But they treated him as an impostor: so an earthquake assailed them; and at morn they were found prostrate and dead in their dwellings

29:38.t: And we destroyed Ad and Themoud. Already is this made plain to you in the ruins of their dwellings. For Satan had made their own works fair seeming to them, and drew them from the right path, keen-sighted though they were

29:39.t: And Corah and Pharaoh and Haman. With proofs of his mission did Moses come to them, and they behaved proudly on the earth; but us they could not outstrip

29:40.t: For, every one of them did we seize in his sin. Against some of them did we send a stone-charged wind: Some of them did the terrible cry of Gabriel surprise: for some of them we cleaved the earth; and some of them we drowned. And it was not God who would deal wrongly by them, but they wronged themselves

29:41.t: The likeness for those who take to themselves guardians instead of God is the likeness of the SPIDER who buildeth her a house: But verily, frailest of all houses surely is the house of the spider. Did they but know this

29:42.t: God truly knoweth all that they call on beside Him; and He is the Mighty, the Wise

29:43.t: These similitudes do we set forth to men: and none understand them except the wise

29:44.t: God hath created the Heavens and the Earth for a serious end. Verily in this is a sign to those who believe

29:45.t: Recite the portions of the Book which have been revealed to thee and discharge the duty of prayer: for prayer restraineth from the filthy and the blame-worthy. And the gravest duty is the remembrance of God; and God knoweth what ye do

29:46.t: Dispute not, unless in kindly sort, with the people of the Book; save with such of them as have dealt wrongfully with you: And say ye, "We believe in what hath been sent down to us and hath been sent down to you. Our God and your God is one, and to him are we self-surrendered"

29:47.t: Thus have we sent down the Book of the Koran to thee: and they to whom we have given the Book of the law believe in it: and of these Arabians there are those who believe in it: and none, save the Infidels, reject our signs

29:48.t: Thou didst not recite any book
before it: with that right hand of thine thou didst not transcribe one: else might they who treat it as a vain thing have justly doubted

29:49.t: But it is a clear sign in the hearts of those whom "the knowledge" hath reached. None except the wicked reject our signs

29:50.t: And they say, "Unless a sign be sent down to him from his Lord...." SAY: Signs are in the power of God alone. I am only a plain spoken warner

29:51.t: Is it not enough for them that we have sent down to thee the Book to be recited to them? In this verily is a mercy and a warning to those who believe

29:52.t: SAY: God is witness enough between me and you. He knoweth all that is in the Heavens and the Earth, and they who believe in vain things and disbelieve in God - these shall be the lost ones

29:53.t: They will challenge thee to hasten the punishment: but had there not been a season fixed for it, that punishment had already come upon them. But it shall overtake them suddenly when they look not for it

29:54.t: They will challenge thee to hasten the punishment: but verily Hell shall be round about the infidels

29:55.t: One day the punishment shall wrap them round, both from above them and from beneath their feet; and God will say, "Taste ye your own doings

29:56.t: O my servants who have believed! Vast truly is my Earth: me, therefore! yea worship me

29:57.t: Every soul shall taste of death. Then to us shall ye return

29:58.t: But those who shall have believed and wrought righteousness will we lodge in gardens with palaces, beneath which the rivers flow. For ever shall they abide therein. How goodly the reward of those who labour

29:59.t: Who patiently endure, and put their trust in their Lord

29:60.t: How many animals are there which provide not their own food! God feedeth them and you. He Heareth, Knoweth all things

29:61.t: If thou ask them who hath created the Heavens and the Earth, and hath imposed laws on the sun and on the moon, they will certainly say, "God." How then can they devise lies

29:62.t: God lavisheth supplies on such of his servants as He pleaseth or giveth to them by measure. God knoweth all things

29:63.t: If thou ask them who sendeth rain from heaven, and by it quickeneth the earth, after it hath been dead, they will certainly answer, "God." SAY: Praise be to God! Yet most of them do not understand

29:64.t: This present life is no other than a pastime and a disport: but truly the future mansion is life indeed! Would that they knew this

29:65.t: Lo! when they embark on shipboard, they call upon God, vowing him sincere worship, but when He bringeth them safe to land, behold they join partners with Him

29:66.t: In our revelation they believe not, yet take their fill of good things. But in the end they shall know their folly

29:67.t: Do they not see that we have established a safe precinct while all around them men are being spoiled? Will they then believe in vain idols, and not own the goodness of God

29:68.t: But who acteth more wrongly than he who deviseth a lie against God, or calls the truth when it hath come to him, a lie? Is there not an abode for the infidels in Hell

29:69.t: And whoso maketh efforts for us, in our ways will we guide them: for God is assuredly with those who do righteous deeds

30:3.t: In a land hard by: But after their defeat they shall defeat their foes

30:4.t: In a few years. First and last is the affair with God. And on that day shall the faithful rejoice

30:5.t: In the aid of their God: He aideth whom He will; and He is the Mighty, the Merciful

30:6.t: It is the promise of God: To his promise God will not be untrue: but most men know it not

30:7.t: They know the outward shews of this life present, but of the next life are they careless

30:8.t: Have they not considered within themselves that God hath not created the Heavens and the Earth and all that is between them but for a serious end, and for a fixed term? But truly most men believe not that they shall meet their Lord

30:9.t: Have they never journeyed through the land, and seen what hath been the end of those who were before them? Mightier were they than these in strength; and they broke up the land, and dwelt in it in greater numbers than they who dwell there now; and their apostles came to them with proofs of their mission: and it was not God who would wrong them, but they wronged themselves

30:10.t: Then evil was the end of the evil doers; because they had treated our signs as lies, and laughed them to scorn

30:11.t: God bringth forth the creation - then causeth it to return again - then to Him shall ye come back

30:12.t: And on the day when the hour shall arrive, the guilty shall be struck dumb for despair

30:13.t: And they shall have no intercessors from among the gods whom they have joined with God, and they shall deny the gods they joined with Him

30:14.t: And on that day when the Hour shall arrive, shall men be separated one from another

30:15.t: And as for those who shall have believed and done the things that are right, they shall enjoy themselves in a flowery mead

30:16.t: But as for those who shall not have believed, but treated our signs and the meeting of the next life as lies, they shall be given over to the torment

30:17.t: Glorify God therefore when ye reach the evening, and when ye rise at morn

30:18.t: And to Him be praise in the Heavens and on the Earth; and at twilight, and when ye rest at noon

30:19.t: He bringeth forth the living out of the dead, and He bringeth forth the dead out of the living: and He quickeneth the earth when dead. Thus is it that ye too shall be brought forth

30:20.t: And one of his signs it is that He hath created you out of dust; then lo! ye become men who spread themselves far and wide

30:21.t: And one of his signs it is, that He hath created wives for you of your own species, that ye may dwell with them, and hath put love and tenderness between you. Herein truly are signs for those who reflect

30:22.t: And among his signs are the creation of the Heavens and of the Earth, and your variety of tongues and colour. Herein truly are signs for all men

30:23.t: And of his signs are your sleep by night and by day, and your goings in quest of his bounties. Herein truly are signs to those who hearken

30:24.t: And of his signs are, that He sheweth you the lightning, a source of awe and hope; and that He sendeth down rain from the heaven and giveth life by it to the earth when dead. Herein truly are signs to those who understand

30:25.t: And of his signs also one is that the Heaven and the Earth stand firm at his bidding: hereafter, when with one summons He shall summon you out of the earth, - lo! forth shall ye come

30:26.t: His, whatsoever is in the Heavens and on the Earth: all are obedient to him

30:27.t: And He it is who bringeth a creature forth, then causeth it to return again; and to him is this most easy. To whatever is loftiest in heaven and earth is He to be likened; and He is the Mighty, the Wise

30:28.t: He setteth forth to you an instance drawn from yourselves. Have ye among the slaves whom your right hands have won, any partner in what we have bestowed on you, so that ye share alike? Fear ye them as ye fear each other?
Thus make we our signs clear to men of understanding

30:29.t: No, ye do not. But the wicked, devoid of knowledge, follow their own desires: and those whom God shall mislead, who shall guide, and who shall be their protector

30:30.t: Set thou thy face then, as a true convert, towards the Faith which God hath made, and for which He hath made man. No change is there in the creation of God. This is the right Faith, but the greater part of men know it not

30:31.t: And be ye turned to Him, and fear Him, and observe prayer, and be not of those who unite gods with God

30:32.t: Of those who have split up their religion, and have become sects, where every party rejoices in what is their own

30:33.t: When some evil toucheth men, they turn to their Lord and call upon him: then when he hath made them taste his mercy, lo, a part of them join other gods with their Lord

30:34.t: Ungrateful for our favours! Enjoy yourselves then. But in the end ye shall know your folly

30:35.t: Have we sent down to them any mandate which speaketh in favour of what they join with God

30:36.t: When we cause men to taste mercy they rejoice in it; but if, for that which their hands have aforetime wrought, evil befall them, they despair

30:37.t: See they not that God bestoweth full supplies on whom He pleaseth and giveth sparingly to whom He pleaseth? Signs truly are there herein to those who believe

30:38.t: To him who is of kin to thee give his due, and to the poor and to the wayfarer: this will be best for those who seek the face of God; and with them it shall be well

30:39.t: Whatever ye put out at usury to increase it with the substance of others shall have no increase from God: but whatever ye shall give in alms, as seeking the face of God, shall be doubled to you

30:40.t: It is God who created you - then fed you - then will cause you to die - then will make you alive. Is there any of your companion-gods who can do aught of these things? Praise be to Him! and far be He exalted above the gods they join with Him

30:41.t: Destruction hath appeared by land and by sea on account of what men's hands have wrought, that it might make them taste somewhat of the fruit of their doings, that haply they might turn to God

30:42.t: SAY: Journey through the land, and see what hath been the end of those who were before you! The greater part of them joined other gods with God

30:43.t: Set thy face then towards the right faith, ere the day come which none can hinder God from bringing on. On that day shall they be parted in twain

30:44.t: Unbelievers on whom shall be their unbelief; and they who have wrought righteousness, and prepared for themselves couches of repose

30:45.t: That of his bounty He may reward those who have believed and wrought righteousness; for the unbelievers He loveth not

30:46.t: And one of his signs is that He sendeth the winds with glad tidings of rain, both that He may cause you to taste his mercy, and that ships may sail at his command, that out of his bounties ye may seek wealth, and that haply ye may render thanks

30:47.t: We have sent apostles before thee to their peoples, and they presented themselves to them with clear proofs of their mission; and while it behoved us to succour the faithful, we took vengeance on the guilty

30:48.t: It is God who sendeth the winds and uplifteth the clouds, and, as He pleaseth, spreadeth them on high, and breaketh them up; and thou mayest see the rain issuing from their midst; and when He poureth it down on such of his servants as He pleaseth, lo! they are filled with joy

30:49.t: Even they who before it was sent down to them, were in mute despair

30:50.t: Look then at the traces of God's mercy - how after its death he quickeneth the earth! This same God will surely quicken the dead, for to all things His might is equal

30:51.t: Yet should we send a blast, and should they see their harvest turn yellow, they would afterwards shew themselves ungrateful

30:52.t: Thou canst not make the dead to hear, neither canst thou make the deaf to hear the call, when they withdraw and turn their backs

30:53.t: Neither canst thou guide the blind out of their error: in sooth, none shalt thou make to hear, save him who shall believe in our signs: for they are resigned to our will

30:54.t: It is God who hath created you in weakness, then after weakness hath given you strength: then after strength, weakness and grey hairs: He createth what He will; and He is the Wise, the Powerful

30:55.t: And on the day whereon the Hour shall arrive, the wicked will swear. That not above an hour have they waited: Even so did they utter lies on earth

30:56.t: But they to whom knowledge and faith have been given will say, "Ye have waited, in accordance with the book of God, till the day of Resurrection: for this is the day of the Resurrection - but ye knew it not

30:57.t: On that day their plea shall not avail the wicked, neither shall they again be bidden to seek acceptance with God

30:58.t: And now have we set before men, in this Koran, every kind of parable: yet if thou bring them a single verse of it, the infidels will surely say, "Ye are only utterers of vain things

30:59.t: It is thus that God hath sealed up the hearts of those who are devoid of knowledge

30:60.t: But do thou, Muhammad, bear with patience, for true is the promise of God; and let not those who have no firm belief, unsettle thee

31:3.t: A guidance and a mercy to the righteous

31:4.t: Who observe prayer, and pay the impost, and believe firmly in the life to come

31:5.t: These rest on guidance from their Lord, and with these it shall be well

31:6.t: But a man there is who buyeth an idle tale, that in his lack of knowledge he may mislead others from the way of God, and turn it to scorn. For such is prepared a shameful punishment

31:7.t: And when our signs are rehearsed to him, he turneth away disdainfully, as though he heard them not, - as though his ears were heavy with deafness. Announce to him therefore tidings of an afflictive punishment

31:8.t: But they who shall have believed and wrought good works, shall enjoy the gardens of delight

31:9.t: For ever shall they dwell therein: it is God's true promise! and He is the Mighty, the Wise

31:10.t: Without pillars that can be seen hath He created the heavens, and on the earth hath thrown mountains lest it should move with you; and He hath scattered over it animals of every sort: and from the Heaven we send down rain and cause every kind of noble plant to grow up therein

31:11.t: This is the creation of God: Shew me now what others than He have created. Ah! the ungodly are in a manifest delusion

31:12.t: Of old we bestowed wisdom upon LOKMAN, and taught him thus - "Be thankful to God: for whoever is thankful, is thankful to his own behoof; and if any shall be thankless... God truly is self-sufficient, worthy of all praise

31:13.t: And bear in mind when Lokman said to his son by way of warning, "O my son! join not other gods with God, for the joining gods with God is the great impiety

31:14.t: We have commanded man concerning his parents. His mother carrieth him with weakness upon weakness; nor until after two years is he weaned. Be grateful to me, and to thy parents. Unto me shall all come

31:15.t: But if they importune thee to join that with Me of which thou hast no knowledge, obey them not: comport thyself towards them in this world as is meet and right; but follow the way of him who turneth unto me. Unto me shall ye return at last, and then will I tell you of your doings

31:16.t: O my son! verily God will bring everything to light, though it were but the weight of a grain of mustard-seed, and hidden in a rock or in the heavens or in the earth; for, God is subtile, informed of all

31:17.t: O my son! observe prayer, and enjoin the right and forbid the wrong, and be patient under whatever shall betide thee: for this is a bounden duty

31:18.t: And distort not thy face at men; nor walk thou loftily on the earth; for God loveth no arrogant vain-glorious one

31:19.t: But let thy pace be middling; and lower thy voice: for the least pleasing of voices is surely the voice of asses

31:20.t: See ye not how that God hath put under you all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, and hath been bounteous to you of his favours, both for soul and body. But some are there who dispute of God without knowledge, and have no guidance and no illuminating Book

31:21.t: And when it is said to them, Follow ye what God hath sent down, they say, "Nay; that religion in which we found our fathers will we follow." What! though Satan bid them to the torment of the flame

31:22.t: But whoso setteth his face toward God with self-surrender, and is a doer of that which is good, hath laid hold on a sure handle; for unto God is the issue of all things

31:23.t: But let not the unbelief of the unbelieving grieve thee: unto us shall they return: then will we tell them of their doings; for God knoweth the very secrets of the breast

31:24.t: Yet a little while will we provide for them: afterwards will we force them to a stern punishment

31:25.t: If thou ask them who hath created the heavens and the earth, they will certainly reply, "God." SAY: God be praised! But most of them have no knowledge

31:26.t: God's, whatever is in the Heavens and the Earth! for God, He is the Rich, the Praiseworthy

31:27.t: If all the trees that are upon the earth were to become pens, and if God should after that swell the sea into seven seas of ink, His words would not be exhausted: for God is Mighty, Wise

31:28.t: Your creation and your quickening hereafter, are but as those of a single individual. Verily, God Heareth, Seeth

31:29.t: Seest thou not that God causeth the night to come in upon the day, and the day to come in upon the night? and that he hath subjected the sun and the moon to laws by which each speedeth along to an appointed goal? and that God therefore is acquainted with that which ye do

31:30.t: This, for that God is the truth; and that whatever ye call upon beside Him is a vain thing; and that God - He is the High, the Great

31:31.t: Seest thou not how the ships speed on in the sea, through the favour of God, that he may shew you of his signs? for herein are signs to all patient, grateful ones

31:32.t: When the waves cover them like dark shadows they call upon God as with sincere religion; but when He safely landeth them, some of them there are who halt between two opinions. Yet none reject our signs but all deceitful, ungrateful ones

31:33.t: O men! fear ye your Lord, and dread the day whereon father shall not atone for son, neither shall a son in the least atone for his father. Aye! the promise of God is a truth. Let not this present life then deceive you; neither let the deceiver deceive you concerning God

31:34.t: Aye! God! - with Him is the knowledge of the Hour: and He sendeth down the rain - and He knoweth what is in the wombs - but no soul knoweth what it shall have gotten on the morrow: neither knoweth any soul in what land it shall die. But God is knowing, informed of all

32:2.t: This Book is without a doubt a Revelation sent down from the Lord of the Worlds

32:3.t: Will they say, He hath forged it? Nay, it is the truth from thy Lord that thou mayest warn a people to whom no warner hath come before thee, that haply they may be guided

32:4.t: God it is who hath created the Heavens and the Earth and all that is between them in six days; then ascended his throne. Save Him ye have no patron, and none to plead for you. Will ye not then reflect

32:5.t: From the Heaven to the Earth He governeth all things: hereafter shall they come up to him on a day whose length shall be a thousand of such years as ye reckon

32:6.t: This is He who knoweth the unseen and the seen; the Mighty, the Merciful

32:7.t: Who hath made everything which he hath created most good; and began the creation of man with clay

32:8.t: Then ordained his progeny from germs of life, from sorry water

32:9.t: Then shaped him, and breathed of His Spirit into him, and gave you hearing and seeing and hearts: what little thanks do ye return

32:10.t: And they say, "What! when we shall have lain hidden in the earth, shall we become a new creation?" Yea, they deny that they shall meet their Lord

32:11.t: SAY: The angel of death who is charged with you shall cause you to die: then shall ye be returned to your Lord

32:12.t: Couldst thou but see when the guilty shall droop their heads before their Lord, and cry, "O our Lord! we have seen and we have heard: return us then to life: we will do that which is right. Verily we believe firmly

32:13.t: Had we pleased we had certainly given to every soul its guidance. But true shall be the word which hath gone forth from me - I will surely fill hell with Djinn and men together

32:14.t: Taste then the recompense of your having forgotten the meeting with this your day. We, too, we have forgotten you: taste then an eternal punishment for that which ye have wrought

32:15.t: They only believe in our signs, who, when mention is made of them, fall down in ADORATION, and celebrate the praise of their Lord, and are not puffed up with disdain

32:16.t: Who, as they raise them from their couches, call on their Lord with fear and desire, and give alms of that with which we have supplied them

32:17.t: No soul knoweth what joy of the eyes is reserved for the good in recompense of their works

32:18.t: Shall he then who is a believer be as he who sinneth grossly? they shall not be held alike

32:19.t: As to those who believe and do that which is right, they shall have gardens of eternal abode as the meed of their works

32:20.t: But as for those who grossly sin, their abode shall be the fire: so oft as they shall desire to escape out of it, back shall they be turned into it. And it shall be said to them, Taste ye the torment of the fire, which ye treated as a lie

32:21.t: And we will surely cause them to taste a punishment yet nearer at hand, besides the greater punishment, that haply they may turn to us in penitence

32:22.t: Who acteth worse than he who is warned by the signs of his Lord, then turneth away from them? We will surely take vengeance on the guilty ones

32:23.t: We heretofore gave the Book of the law to Moses: have thou no doubt as to our meeting with him: and we appointed it for the guidance of the children of Israel

32:24.t: And we appointed Imams from among them who should guide after our command when they had themselves endured with constancy, and had firmly believed in our signs

32:25.t: Now thy Lord! He will decide between them on the day of resurrection as to the subject of their disputes

32:26.t: Is it not notorious to them how many generations, through whose abodes they walk, we have destroyed before them? Truly herein are sings: will they not then hear

32:27.t: See they not how we drive the rain to some parched land and thereby bring forth corn of which their cattle and themselves do eat? Will they not then behold

32:28.t: They say, "When will this decision take place? Tell us, if ye are men of truth

32:29.t: SAY: On the day of that decision, the faith of infidels shall not avail them, and they shall have no further respite

32:30.t: Stand aloof from them then, and wait thou, for they too wait

33:1.t: O PROPHET, fear thou God, and obey not the unbelievers and the hypocrites; - Truly God is Knowing, Wise

33:2.t: But follow what is revealed to thee from thy Lord: Cognisant truly is He of all your actions

33:3.t: And put thou thy trust in God, for a sufficient guardian is God

33:4.t: God hath not given a man two hearts within him; neither hath he made your wives whom ye divorce to be as your mothers; nor hath he made your adopted sons to be as your own sons. Such words are indeed in your mouths; but God speaketh the truth, and in the right way He guideth

33:5.t: Name them after their fathers: this will be more right before God. But if ye know not who their fathers are, then let them be your brethren in the faith, and your comrades. And unless made with intent of heart, mistakes in this matter shall be no crime in you: for God is Lenient, Merciful

33:6.t: Nearer of kin to the faithful is the Prophet, than they are to their own selves. His wives are their mothers. According to the Book of God, they who are related by blood, are nearer the one to the other than other believers, and than those who have fled their country for the cause of God: but whatever kindness ye shew to your kindred, shall be noted down in the Book

33:7.t: And remember that we have entered into covenant with the Prophets, and with thee, and with Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus, Son of Mary: and we formed with them a strict covenant

33:8.t: That God may question the men of truth as to their truth. But a sore torment hath He prepared for the unbelievers

33:9.t: O believers! remember the goodness of God towards you, when the armies came against you, and we sent against them a blast, and hosts that ye saw not; for the eye of God was upon your doings

33:10.t: When they assailed you from above you, and from below you, and when your eyes became distracted, and your hearts came up into your throat, and ye thought divers thoughts of God

33:11.t: Then were the faithful tried, and with strong quaking did they quake

33:12.t: And when the disaffected and the diseased of heart said, "God and his Apostle have made us but a cheating promise

33:13.t: And when a party of them said, "O people of Yathrib! there is no place of safety for you here; therefore return into the city." And another party of you asked the prophet's leave to return, saying, "Our houses are left defenceless." No! they were not left defenceless: but their sole thought was to flee away

33:14.t: If the enemy had effected an entry at all points, and they
had been asked to promote confusion, they would have done so; but only a short time would they have remained in it. -

33:15.t: They had before pledged themselves to God that they would not turn their backs; and a pledge given to God must be enquired of

33:16.t: SAY: Flight shall not profit you; if ye have fled the death or the slaughter, yet even then, but a little while shall ye enjoy your good things

33:17.t: SAY: Who is he that will screen you from God, whether He choose to bring evil on you, or to shew you mercy? None beside God shall they find to be their patron or helper

33:18.t: God well knoweth those among you who cause hindrances, and those who say to their brethren, "Come hither to us;" and who come not to the fight except a little

33:19.t: It is out of covetousness in your regard: for when an alarm cometh, thou mayest see them look to thee, and roll their eyes like him on whom the shadows of death have fallen! Yet, when the alarm is passed, with sharp tongues will they assail you, covetous of the best of the spoil. No faith have these! God will make their doings of no avail! And easy is this with God

33:20.t: They thought that the CONFEDERATES would never retire; and were the confederates to come again, they would fain be dwelling among the Arabs of the desert, and there ask news about you! for though they were with you, they fought not except a little

33:21.t: A noble pattern had ye in God's Apostle, for all who hope in God, and in the latter day, and oft remember God

33:22.t: And when the faithful saw the confederates, they said, "This is what God and His Apostle promised us, and God and His Apostle spoke truly:" and it only increased their faith and self-devotion

33:23.t: Some were there among the faithful who made good what they had promised to God. Some have fulfilled their course, and others await its fulfilment, and have not been changelings who change

33:24.t: That God may reward the faithful for their faithfulness, and may punish the hypocrites, if He so please, or be turned unto them: for God is Forgiving, Merciful

33:25.t: And God drove back the infidels in their wrath; they won no advantage; God sufficed the faithful in the fight: for God is Strong, Mighty

33:26.t: And He caused those of the people of the Book
, who had aided the confederates, to come down out of their fortresses, and cast dismay into their hearts: some ye slew, others ye took prisoners

33:27.t: And He gave you their land, and their dwellings, and their wealth, for an heritage - even a land on which ye had never set foot: for the might of God is equal to all things

33:28.t: O Prophet! say to thy wives, If ye desire this present life and its braveries, come then, I will provide for you, and dismiss you with an honourable dismissal

33:29.t: But if ye desire God and His Apostle, and a home in the next life, then, truly, hath God prepared for those of you who are virtuous, a great reward

33:30.t: O wives of the Prophet! should any of you be guilty of a proven lewdness, doubly shall her chastisement be doubled: and with God this is easy

33:31.t: But whoever of you shall obey God and His Apostle, and shall do that which is right, twice over will we give her her reward, and we have prepared for her a noble provision

33:32.t: O wives of the Prophet! ye are not as other women. If ye fear God, be not too complaisant of speech, lest the man of unhealthy heart should lust after you, but speak with discreet speech

33:33.t: And abide still in your houses, and go not in public decked as in the days of your former ignorance, but observe prayer, and pay the impost, and obey God and the Apostle: for God only desireth to put away filthiness from you as his household, and with cleansing to cleanse you

33:34.t: And recollect what is rehearsed to you in your houses of the Book of God, and of wisdom: for God is keen-sighted, cognisant of all

33:35.t: Truly the men who resign themselves to God

, and the women who resign themselves, and the believing men and the believing women, and the devout men and the devout women, and the men of truth, and the women of truth, and the patient men and the patient women, and the humble men and the humble women, and the men who give alms and the women who give alms, and the men who fast and the women who fast, and the chaste men and the chaste women, and the men and the women who oft remember God: for them hath God prepared forgiveness and a rich recompense

33:36.t: And it is not for a believer, man or woman, to have any choice in their affairs, when God and His Apostle have decreed a matter: and whoever disobeyeth God and His Apostle, erreth with palpable error

33:37.t: And, remember, when thou saidst to him unto whom God had shewn favour, and to whom thou also hadst shewn favour, "Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear God;" and thou didst hide in thy mind what God would bring to light. and thou didst fear man; but more right had it been to fear God. And when Zaid had settled concerning her to divorce her, we married her to thee, that it might not be a crime in the faithful to marry the wives of their adopted sons, when they have settled the affair concerning them. And the behest of God is to be performed

33:38.t: No blame attacheth to the prophet where God hath given him a permission. Such was the way of God with those prophets who flourished before thee; for God's behest is a fixed decree

33:39.t: Who fulfilled the mission with which God had charged them, and feared Him, and feared none but God. And God taketh a sufficient account

33:40.t: Muhammad is not the father of any man among you, but he is the Apostle of God, and the seal of the prophets: and God knoweth all things

33:41.t: O Believers! remember God with frequent remembrance

33:42.t: and praise Him morning and evening

33:43.t: He blesseth you, and His angels intercede for you, that He may bring you forth out of darkness into light: and Merciful is He to the Believers

33:44.t: Their greeting on the day when they shall meet Him shall be "Peace!" And He hath got ready for them a noble recompense

33:45.t: O Prophet! we have sent thee to be a witness, and a herald of glad tidings, and a warner

33:46.t: And one who, through His own permission, summoneth to God, and a light-giving torch

33:47.t: Announce, therefore, to believers, that great boons do await them from God

33:48.t: And obey not the Infidels and Hypocrites - yet abstain from injuring them: and put thou thy trust in God, for God is a sufficient guardian

33:49.t: O Believers! when ye marry believing women, and then divorce them before ye have consummated the marriage, ye have no term prescribed you, which ye must fulfil towards them: provide for them, and dismiss them with a reputable dismissal

33:50.t: O Prophet! we allow thee thy wives whom thou hast dowered, and the slaves whom thy right hand possesseth out of the booty which God hath granted thee, and the daughters of thy uncle, and of thy paternal and maternal aunts who fled with thee to Medina, and any believing woman who hath given herself up to the Prophet, if the Prophet desired to wed her - a Privilege for thee above the rest of the Faithful. We well know what we have settled for them, in regard to their wives and to the slaves whom their right hands hold, that there may be no fault on thy part: and God is Indulgent, Merciful

33:51.t: Thou mayst decline for the present whom thou wilt of them, and thou mayest take to thy bed her whom thou wilt, and whomsoever thou shalt long for of those thou shalt have before neglected; and this shall not be a crime in thee. Thus will it be easier to give them the desire of their eyes, and not to put them to grief, and to satisfy them with what thou shalt accord to each of them. God knoweth what is in your hearts, and God is Knowing, Gracious

33:52.t: It is not permitted thee to take other wives hereafter, nor to change thy present wives for other women, though their beauty charm thee, except slaves whom thy right hand shall possess. And God watcheth all things

33:53.t: O Believers! enter not into the houses of the Prophet, save by his leave, for a meal, without waiting his time. When ye are invited then enter, and when ye have eaten then disperse at once. And engage not in familiar talk, for this would cause the Prophet trouble, and he would be ashamed to bid you go; but God is not ashamed to say the truth. And when ye would ask any gift of his wives, ask it from behind a veil. Purer will this be for your hearts and for their hearts. And ye must not trouble the Apostle of God, nor marry his wives, after him, for ever. This would be a grave offence with God

33:54.t: Whether ye bring a matter to the light or hide it, God truly hath knowledge of all things

33:55.t: No blame shall attach to them

for speaking to their fathers unveiled, or to their sons, or to their brothers, or to their brothers' sons, or to their sisters' sons, or to their women, or to the slaves whom their right hands hold. And fear ye God: for God witnesseth all things

33:56.t: Verily, God and His Angels bless the Prophet! Bless ye Him, O Believers, and salute Him with salutations of Peace

33:57.t: Verily, they who affront God and His Apostle, the curse of God is on them in this world, and in the world to come: and He hath prepared for them a shameful chastisement

33:58.t: And they who shall affront believing men and believing women, for no fault of theirs, they shall surely bear the guilt of slander, and of a clear wrong

33:59.t: O Prophet! speak to thy wives and to thy daughters, and to the wives of the Faithful, that they let their veils fall low. Thus will they more easily be known, and they will not be affronted. God is Indulgent, Merciful

33:60.t: If the Hypocrites, and the men of tainted heart, and the stirrers of sedition in Medina desist not, we will surely stir thee up against them. Then shall they not be suffered to dwell near thee therein, but a little while

33:61.t: Cursed wherever they are found; they shall be seized and slain with slaughter

33:62.t: Such hath been the way of God with those who lived before them; and no change canst thou find in the way of God

33:63.t: Men will ask thee of "the Hour." SAY: The knowledge of it is with God alone: and who can tell thee whether haply the Hour be not nigh at hand

33:64.t: Verily, God hath cursed the Infidels, and hath got ready for them the flame

33:65.t: For aye shall they abide therein; none to befriend them, no helper shall they find

33:66.t: On the day when their faces shall be rolled in the fire, they shall cry: "Oh! would that we had obeyed God, and obeyed the Apostle

33:67.t: And they shall say: "Oh our Lord! indeed we obeyed our chiefs and our great ones, and they misled us from the way of God

33:68.t: O our Lord! give them a double chastisement, and curse them with a heavy curse

33:69.t: O Believers! be not like those who affronted Moses. But God cleared him from what they said of him, and of God was he highly esteemed

33:70.t: O Believers! fear God, and speak with well-guided speech

33:71.t: That God may bless your doings for you, and forgive you your sins. And whoso obeyeth God and His Apostle with great bliss shall be blessed

33:72.t: Verily, we proposed to the Heavens, and to the Earth, and to the Mountains to receive the Faith, but they refused the burden, and they feared to receive it. Man undertook to bear it, but hath proved unjust, senseless

33:73.t: Therefore will God punish the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women, and the men and the women who join gods with God; but to the believing men and women will God turn him: for God is Indulgent, Merciful

34:1.t: PRAISE be to God! to whom belongeth all that is in the Heavens and all that is on the Earth; and to Him be praise in the next world: for he is the All-wise, the All-informed

34:2.t: He knoweth what entereth into the earth, and what proceedeth from it; and what cometh down from heaven, and what goeth up into it: and He is the Merciful, the Forgiving

34:3.t: Never," say the unbelievers, "will the Hour come upon us!" SAY: Yea, by my Lord who knoweth the unseen, it will surely come upon you! not the weight of a mote either in the Heavens or in the Earth escapeth him; nor is there aught less than this or aught greater, which is not in the clear Book

34:4.t: To the intent that God may reward those who have believed and done the things that are right: Pardon and a noble provision shall they receive

34:5.t: But as for those who aim to invalidate our signs, - a chastisement of painful torment awaiteth them

34:6.t: And they to whom knowledge hath been given see that what hath been sent down to thee from thy Lord is the truth, and that it guideth into the way of the Glorious one, the Praiseworthy

34:7.t: But the unbelievers say to those whom they fall in with, "Shall we shew you a man who will foretell you that when ye shall have been utterly torn and rent to pieces, ye shall be restored in a new form

34:8.t: He deviseth a lie about God, or there is a djinn in him," but they who believe not in the next life, shall incur the chastisement, and be lost in the mazes of estrangement from God

34:9.t: What! have they never contemplated that which is before them and behind them, the Heaven and the Earth? If such were our pleasure, we could sink them into that Earth, or cause a portion of that Heaven to fall upon them! herein truly is a sign for our every returning servant

34:10.t: Of old bestowed we on David a gift, our special boon: - "Ye mountains and ye birds answer his songs of praise." And we made the iron soft for him

34:11.t: Make coats of mail, and arrange its plates; and work ye righteousness; for I behold your actions

34:12.t: And unto Solomon did we subject the wind, which travelled in the morning a month's journey, and a month's journey in the evening. And we made a fountain of molten brass to flow for him. And of the Djinn were some who worked in his presence, by the will of his Lord; and such of them as swerved from our bidding will we cause to taste the torment of the flame

34:13.t: They made for him whatever he pleased, of lofty halls, and images, and dishes large as tanks for watering camels, and cooking pots that stood firmly. "Work," said we, "O family of David with thanksgiving:" But few of my servants are the thankful

34:14.t: And when we decreed the death of Solomon, nothing shewed them that he was dead but a reptile of the earth that gnawed the staff which supported his corpse. And when it fell, the Djinn perceived that if they had known the things unseen, they had not continued in this shameful affliction

34:15.t: A sign there was to SABA, in their dwelling places: - two gardens, the one on the right hand and the other on the left: - "Eat ye of your Lord's supplies, and give thanks to him: Goodly is the country, and gracious is the Lord

34:16.t: But they turned aside: so we sent upon them the flood of Irem; and we changed them their gardens into two gardens of bitter fruit and tamarisk and some few jujube trees

34:17.t: Such was our retribution on them for their ingratitude: but do we thus recompense any except the ungrateful

34:18.t: And we placed between them and the cities which we have blessed, conspicuous cities, and we fixed easy stages: "Travel ye through them by night and day, secure

34:19.t: But they said, "O Lord! make the distance between our journeys longer," - and against themselves did they act unjustly: so we made them a tale, and scattered them with an utter scattering. Truly herein are signs to everyone that is patient, grateful

34:20.t: And Eblis found that he had judged truly of them: and they all except a remnant of the faithful, followed him

34:21.t: Yet no power had he over them. Only we would discern him who believed in the life to come, from him who doubted of it; for thy Lord watcheth all things

34:22.t: SAY: Call ye upon those whom ye deem gods, beside God: their power in the Heavens and in the Earth is not the weight of an atom - neither have they any share in either; nor hath He a helper from among them

34:23.t: No intercession shall avail with Him but that which He shall Himself allow. Until when at last their hearts shall be relieved from terror, they shall say, "What saith your Lord?" they shall say, "The Truth; and He is the High, the Great

34:24.t: SAY: Who supplieth you out of the Heavens and the Earth? SAY: God. And either we or ye have guidance, or are in palpable error

34:25.t: SAY: Not as to our faults shall ye be questioned; neither shall we be questioned as to your actions

34:26.t: SAY: Our Lord will gather us together: then will He judge between us in justice; for He is the Judge, the Knowing

34:27.t: SAY: Shew me those whom ye have united with Him as associates: Nay, rather, He is God, the Mighty, the Wise

34:28.t: And we have sent thee to mankind at large, to announce and to threaten. But most men understand not

34:29.t: And they say, "When will this threat come to pass? Tell us, if ye be men of truth

34:30.t: SAY: Ye are menaced with a day, which not for an hour shall ye retard or hasten on

34:31.t: The unbelievers say, "We will not believe in this Koran, nor in the Books which preceded it." But couldst thou see when the wicked shall be set before their Lord! With reproaches will they answer one another. The weak shall say to the mighty ones, "But for you we had been believers

34:32.t: Then shall the mighty ones say to the weak, "What! was it we who turned you aside from the guidance which had reached you? Nay, but ye acted wickedly yourselves

34:33.t: And the weak shall say to the mighty ones, "Nay, but there was a plot by night and by day, when ye bad us believe not in God, and gave him peers." And they shall proclaim their repentance after they have seen the punishment! And yokes will we place on the necks of those who have not believed! Shall they be rewarded but as they have wrought

34:34.t: And never have we sent a warner to any city whose opulent men did not say, "In sooth we disbelieve your message

34:35.t: And they said, "We are the more abundant in riches and in children, nor shall we be among the punished

34:36.t: SAY: Of a truth my Lord will be liberal or sparing in his supplies to whom he pleaseth: but the greater part of men acknowledge it not

34:37.t: Neither by your riches nor by your children shall you bring yourselves into nearness with Us; but they who believe and do the thing that is right shall have a double reward for what they shall have done: and in the pavilions of Paradise shall they dwell secure

34:38.t: But they who shall aim to invalidate our signs, shall be consigned to punishment

34:39.t: SAY: Of a truth my Lord will be liberal in supplies to whom he pleaseth of his servants, or will be sparing to him: and whatever ye shall give in alms he will return; and He is the best dispenser of gifts

34:40.t: One day he will gather them all together: then shall he say to the angels, "Did these worship you

34:41.t: They shall say, "Glory be to thee! Thou art our master, not these! But they worshipped the Djinn: it was in them that most of them believed

34:42.t: On this day the one of you shall have no power over others for help or hurt. And we will say to the evil doers, "Taste ye the torment of the fire, which ye treated as a delusion

34:43.t: For when our distinct signs are recited to them, they say, "This is merely a man who would fain pervert you from your father's Worship." And they say, "This
is no other than a forged falsehood." And the unbelievers say to the truth when it is presented to them, "Tis nothing but palpable sorcery

34:44.t: Yet have we given them no books in which to study deeply, nor have we sent any one to them before thee, charged with warnings

34:45.t: They also flourished before them, treated our apostles as impostors in like sort: but not to the tenth part of what we bestowed on them, have these attained. And yet when they charged my apostles with deceit, how terrible was my vengeance

34:46.t: SAY: One thing in sooth do I advise you: - that ye stand up before God two and two, or singly, and then reflect that in your fellow citizen is no djinn: he is no other than your warner before a severe punishment

34:47.t: SAY: I ask not any wage from you: keep it for yourselves: my wage is from God alone. And He is witness over all things

34:48.t: SAY: Truly my Lord sendeth forth the Truth: - Knower of things unseen

34:49.t: SAY: Truth is come, and falsehood shall vanish and return no more

34:50.t: SAY: If I err, verily to my own cost only shall I err: but if I have guidance, it will be of my Lord's revealing, for He is the Hearer, the near at hand

34:51.t: Couldst thou see how they shall tremble and find no escape, and be taken forth from the place that is so near

34:52.t: And shall say, "We believe in Him!" But how, in their present distance, shall they receive the faith

34:53.t: When they had before denied it, and aimed their shafts at the mysteries from afar

34:54.t: And a gulf shall be between them and that which they shall desire - As was done unto their likes of old, who were lost in the questionings of doubt

35:1.t: PRAISE be to God, Maker of the Heavens and of the Earth! Who employeth the ANGELS as envoys, with pairs of wings, two, three, and four: He addeth to his creature what He will! Truly God hath power for all things

35:2.t: The mercy which God layeth open for man, no one can keep back; and what He shall keep back, none can afterwards send forth. And He is the Mighty, the Wise

35:3.t: O men! bear in mind the favour of God towards you. Is there a creator other than God, who nourisheth you with the gifts of heaven and earth? There is no God but He! How then are ye turned aside from Him

35:4.t: If they treat thee as an impostor, then before thee have apostles been treated as impostors. But to God shall all things return

35:5.t: O men! assuredly the promise of God is true: let not then the present life deceive you: and let not the Deceiver deceive you as to God

35:6.t: Yes, Satan is your foe. For a foe then hold him. He calleth his followers to him that they may become inmates of the flame

35:7.t: The unbelievers, - for them a terrible punishment! But believers and doers of good works, for them is mercy, and a great reward

35:8.t: Shall he, the evil of whose deeds are so tricked out to him that he deemeth them good, be treated like him who seeth things aright? Verily God misleadeth whom He will, and guideth whom He will. Spend not thy soul in sighs for them: God knoweth their doings

35:9.t: It is God who sendeth forth the winds which raise the clouds aloft: then drive we them on to some land dead from drought, and give life thereby to the earth after its death. So shall be the resurrection

35:10.t: If any one desireth greatness, all greatness is in God. The good word riseth up to Him, and the righteous deed will He exalt. But a severe punishment awaiteth the plotters of evil things; and the plots of such will He render vain

35:11.t: Moreover, God created you of dust - then of the germs of life - then made you two sexes: and no female conceiveth or bringeth forth without his knowledge; and the aged ageth not, nor is aught minished from man's age, but in accordance with the Book. An easy thing truly is this to God

35:12.t: Nor are the two seas alike: the one fresh, sweet, pleasant for drink, and the other salt, bitter; yet from both ye eat fresh fish, and take forth for you ornaments to wear, and thou seest the ships cleaving their waters that ye may go in quest of his bounties, and that ye may be thankful

35:13.t: He causeth the night to enter in upon the day, and the day to enter in upon the night; and He hath given laws to the sun and to the moon, so that each journeyeth to its appointed goal: This is God your Lord: All power is His: But the gods whom ye call on beside Him have no power over the husk of a date stone

35:14.t: If ye cry to them they will not hear your cry; and if they heard they would not answer you, and in the day of resurrection they will disown your joining them with God: and none can instruct thee like Him who is informed of all

35:15.t: O men! ye are but paupers in need of God; but God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy

35:16.t: If He please, He could sweep you away, and bring forth a new creation

35:17.t: Nor will this be hard for God

35:18.t: And the burdened soul shall not bear the burden of another: and if the heavy laden soul cry out for its burden to be carried, yet shall not aught of it be carried, even by the near of kin! Thou shalt warn those who fear their Lord in secret, and observe prayer. And whoever shall keep himself pure, he purifieth himself to his own behoof: for unto God shall be the final gathering

35:19.t: And the blind and the seeing are not alike

35:21.t: nor the shade and the hot wind

35:22.t: Nor are the living and the dead the same thing! God indeed shall make whom He will to hearken, but thou shalt not make those who are in their graves to hearken

35:23.t: for only with warning art thou charged

35:24.t: Verily we have sent thee with the truth; a bearer of good tidings and a warner; nor hath there been a people unvisited by its warner

35:25.t: And if they treat thee as a liar, so did those who were before them threat their Apostles who came to them with the proofs of their mission, and with the Scriptures and with the enlightening Book

35:26.t: Then chastised I the unbelievers: and how great was my vengeance

35:27.t: Seest thou not how that God sendeth down water from the Heaven, and that by it we cause the up-growth of fruits of varied hues, and that on the mountains are tracks of varied hues, white and red, and others are of a raven black

35:28.t: And of men and reptiles and animals, various likewise are the hues. Such only of his servants as are possessed of knowledge fear God. Lo! God is Mighty, Gracious

35:29.t: Verily they who recite the Book of God, and observe prayer, and give alms in public and in private from what we have bestowed upon them, may hope for a merchandise that shall not perish

35:30.t: God will certainly pay them their due wages, and of his bounty increase them: for He is Gracious, Grateful

35:31.t: And that which we have revealed to thee of the Book is the very Truth, confirmatory of previous Scriptures: for God knoweth and beholdeth his servants

35:32.t: Moreover, we have made the Book an heritage to those of our servants whom we have chosen. Some of them injure themselves by evil deeds; others keep the midway between good and evil; and others, by the permission of God, outstrip in goodness; this is the great merit

35:33.t: Into the gardens of Eden shall they enter: with bracelets of gold and pearl shall they be decked therein, and therein shall their raiment be of silk

35:34.t: And they shall say, "Praise be to God who hath put away sorrow from us. Verily our Lord is Gracious, Grateful

35:35.t: Who of His bounty hath placed us in a mansion that shall abide for ever: therein no toil shall reach us, and therein no weariness shall touch us

35:36.t: But for infidels is the fire of Hell; to die shall never be decreed them, nor shall aught of its torment be made light to them. Thus reward we every infidel

35:37.t: And therein shall they cry aloud, "Take us hence, O our Lord! righteousness will we work, and not what we wrought of old." - "Prolonged we not your days that whoever would be warned might be warned therein? And the preacher came to you - Taste it then." - There is no protector for the unjust

35:38.t: God truly knoweth the hidden things both of the Heavens and of the Earth: for He knoweth the very secrets of the breast

35:39.t: He hath appointed you his vicegerents in the earth: And whoever believeth not, on him shall be his unbelief; and their unbelief shall only increase for the unbelievers, hatred at the hands of their Lord: - and their unbelief shall only increase for the unbelievers their own perdition

35:40.t: SAY: What think ye of the gods whom ye invoke beside God? Shew me what part of the earth they have created? Had they a share in the creation of the Heavens? Have we given them a Book in which they can find proofs that they are to be called on? Nay, the wicked promise one another only deceits

35:41.t: Verily God holdeth fast the Heavens and the Earth that they pass not away: and if they were passing away none could hold them back but He: for He is Kind, Gracious

35:42.t: They swore by God with their mightiest oath that should a preacher come to them they would yield to guidance more than any people: but when the preacher came to them it only increased in them their estrangement

35:43.t: Their haughtiness on earth and their plotting of evil! But the plotting of evil shall only enmesh those who make use of it. Look they then for aught but God's way of dealing with the peoples of old? Thou shalt not find any change in the way of God, - Yea, thou shalt not find any variableness in the way of God

35:44.t: Have they never journeyed in the land and seen what hath been the end of those who flourished before them, though mightier in strength than they? God is not to be frustrated by aught in the Heavens or in the Earth; for He is the All-knowing, the All-mighty

35:45.t: If, moreover, God should chastise men according to their deserts, He would not leave even a reptile on the back of the earth! But to an appointed time doth He respite them. And when their time shall come, then verily God's eye is on his servants

36:3.t: Surely of the Sent Ones, Thou

36:5.t: A revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful

36:6.t: That thou shouldest warn a people whose fathers were not warned and therefore lived in heedlessness

36:7.t: Just, now, is our sentence against most of them; therefore they shall not believe

36:8.t: On their necks have we placed chains which reach the chin, and forced up are their heads

36:9.t: Before them have we set a barrier and behind them a barrier, and we have shrouded them in a veil, so that they shall not see

36:10.t: Alike is it to them if thou warn them or warn them not: they will not believe

36:11.t: Him only shalt thou really warn, who followeth the monition and feareth the God of mercy in secret: him cheer with tidings of pardon, and of a noble recompense

36:12.t: Verily, it is We who will quicken the dead, and write down the works which they have sent on before them, and the traces which they shall have left behind them: and everything have we set down in the clear Book of our decrees

36:13.t: Set forth to them the instance of the people of the city when the Sent Ones came to it

36:14.t: When we sent two unto them and they charged them both with imposture - therefore with a third we strengthened them: and they said, "Verily we are the Sent unto you of God

36:15.t: They said, "Ye are only men like us: Nought hath the God of Mercy sent down. Ye do nothing but lie

36:16.t: They said, "Our Lord knoweth that we are surely sent unto you

36:17.t: To proclaim a clear message is our only duty

36:18.t: They said, "Of a truth we augur ill from you: if ye desist not we will surely stone you, and a grievous punishment will surely befall you from us

36:19.t: They said, "Your augury of ill is with yourselves. Will ye be warned? Nay, ye are an erring people

36:20.t: Then from the end of the city a man came running: He said, "O my people! follow the Sent Ones

36:21.t: Follow those who ask not of you a recompense, and who are rightly guided

36:22.t: And why should I not worship Him who made me, and to whom ye shall be brought back

36:23.t: Shall I take gods beside Him? If the God of Mercy be pleased to afflict me, their intercession will not avert from me aught, nor will they deliver

36:24.t: Truly then should I be in a manifest error

36:25.t: Verily, in your Lord have I believed; therefore hear me

36:26.t: It was said to him, "Enter thou into Paradise:" And he said, "Oh that my people knew

36:27.t: How gracious God hath been to me, and that He hath made me one of His honoured ones

36:28.t: But no army sent we down out of heaven after his death, nor were we then sending down our angels

36:29.t: There was but one shout from Gabriel, and lo! they were extinct

36:30.t: Oh! the misery that rests upon my servants! No apostle cometh to them but they laugh him to scorn

36:31.t: See they not how many generations we have destroyed before them? Not to false gods is it that they shall be brought back

36:32.t: But all, gathered together, shall be set before Us

36:33.t: Moreover, the dead earth is a sign to them: we quicken it and bring forth the grain from it, and they eat thereof

36:34.t: And we make in it gardens of the date and vine; and we cause springs to gush forth in it

36:35.t: That they may eat of its fruits and of the labour of their hands. Will they not therefore be thankful

36:36.t: Glory be to Him, who hath created all the sexual pairs of such things as Earth produceth, and of mankind themselves; and of things beyond their ken

36:37.t: A sign to them also is the Night. We withdraw the day from it, and lo! they are plunged in darkness

36:38.t: And the Sun hasteneth to her place of rest. This, the ordinance of the Mighty, the Knowing

36:39.t: And as for the Moon, We have decreed stations for it, till it change like an old and crooked palm branch

36:40.t: To the Sun it is not given to overtake the Moon, nor doth the night outstrip the day; but each in its own sphere doth journey on

36:41.t: It is also a sign to them that we bare their posterity in the full-laden Ark

36:42.t: And that we have made for them vessels like it on which they embark

36:43.t: And if we please, we drown them, and there is none to help them, and they are not rescued

36:44.t: Unless through our mercy, and that they may enjoy themselves for yet awhile

36:45.t: And when it is said to them, Fear what is before you and what is behind you, that ye may obtain mercy

36:46.t: Aye, not one sign from among the signs of their Lord dost thou bring them, but they turn away from it

36:47.t: And when it is said to them, Give alms of what God hath bestowed on you, they who believe not say to the believers, "Shall we feed him whom God can feed if He will? Truly ye are in no other than a plain error

36:48.t: And they say, "When will this promise be fulfilled, if what ye say be true

36:49.t: They await but a single blast: as they are wrangling shall it assail them

36:50.t: And not a bequest shall they be able to make, nor to their families shall they return

36:51.t: And the trumpet shall be blown, and, lo! they shall speed out of their sepulchres to their Lord

36:52.t: They shall say, "Oh! woe to us! who hath roused us from our sleeping place? 'Tis what the God of Mercy promised; and the Apostles spake the truth

36:53.t: But one blast shall there be, and, lo! they shall be assembled before us, all together

36:54.t: And on that day shall no soul be wronged in the least: neither shall ye be rewarded but as ye shall have wrought

36:55.t: But joyous on that day shall be the inmates of Paradise, in their employ

36:56.t: In shades, on bridal couches reclining, they and their spouses

36:57.t: Therein shall they have fruits, and shall have whatever they require

36:58.t: Peace!" shall be the word on the part of a merciful Lord

36:59.t: But be ye separated this day, O ye sinners

36:60.t: Did I not enjoin on you, O sons of Adam, 'Worship not Satan, for that he is your declared foe

36:61.t: But 'Worship Me: this is a right path

36:62.t: But now hath he led a vast host of you astray. Did ye not then comprehend

36:63.t: This is Hell with which ye were threatened

36:64.t: Endure its heat this day, for that ye believed not

36:65.t: On that day will we set a seal upon their mouths; yet shall their hands speak unto us, and their feet shall bear witness of that which they shall have done

36:66.t: And, if we pleased, we would surely put out their eyes: yet even then would they speed on with rivalry in their path: but how should they see

36:67.t: And, if we pleased, we would surely transform them as they stand, and they would not be able to move onward, or to return

36:68.t: Him cause we to stoop through age whose days we lengthen. Will they not understand

36:69.t: poetry, nor would it beseem him. This Book is no other than a warning and a clear Koran

36:70.t: To warn whoever liveth; and, that against the Infidels sentence may be justly given

36:71.t: See they not that we have created for them among the things which our hands have wrought, the animals of which they are masters

36:72.t: And that we have subjected them unto them? And on some they ride, and of others they eat

36:73.t: And they find in them profitable uses and beverages

36:74.t: Yet have they taken other gods beside God that they might be helpful to them

36:75.t: No power have they to succour them: yet are their votaries an army at their service

36:76.t: Let not their speech grieve thee: We know what they hide and what they bring to light

36:77.t: Doth not man perceive that we have created him of the moist germs of life? Yet lo! is he an open caviller

36:78.t: And he meeteth us with arguments, and forgetteth his creation: "Who," saith he, "shall give life to bones when they are rotten

36:79.t: SAY: He shall give life to them who gave them being at first, for in all creation is he skilled

36:80.t: Who even out of the green tree hath given you fire, and lo! ye kindle flame from it

36:81.t: What! must not He who hath created the Heavens and the Earth be mighty enough to create your likes? Yes! and He is the skilful creator

36:82.t: His command when He willeth aught, is but to say to it, BE, and IT IS

36:83.t: So glory be to Him in whose hand is sway over all things! And to Him shall ye be brought back

37:1.t: By the angels ranged in order for Songs of Praise

37:2.t: And by those who repel demons

37:3.t: And by those who recite the Koran for warning

37:4.t: Truly your God is but one

37:5.t: Lord of the Heavens and of the Earth, and of all that is between them, and Lord of the East

37:6.t: We have adorned the lower heaven with the adornment of the stars

37:7.t: They serve also as a guard against every rebellious Satan

37:8.t: That they overhear not what passeth in the assembly on high, for they are darted at from every side

37:9.t: Driven off and consigned to a lasting torment

37:10.t: While, if one steal a word by stealth, a glistening flame pursueth him

37:11.t: Ask the Meccans then, Are they, or the angels whom we have made, the stronger creation? Aye, of coarse clay have we created them

37:12.t: But while thou marvellest they mock

37:13.t: When they are warned, no warning do they take

37:14.t: And when they see a sign, they fall to mocking

37:15.t: And say, "This is no other than clear sorcery

37:16.t: What! when dead, and turned to dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised

37:17.t: Our sires also of olden times

37:18.t: Say, Yes; and ye shall be covered with disgrace

37:19.t: For, one blast only, and lo! they shall gaze around them

37:20.t: And shall say, "Oh! woe to us! this is the day of reckoning

37:21.t: This is the day of decision which ye gainsaid as an untruth

37:22.t: Gather together those who have acted unjustly, and their consorts, and the gods whom they adored

37:23.t: Beside God; and guide them to the road for Hell

37:24.t: Set them forth: they shall be questioned

37:25.t: How now, that ye help not one another

37:26.t: But on this day they shall submit themselves to God

37:27.t: And shall address one another with mutual reproaches

37:28.t: They shall say, "In sooth, ye came to us in well-omened sort

37:29.t: But they will answer, "Nay, it was ye who would not believe

37:30.t: and we had no power whatever over you. Nay, ye were people given to transgress

37:31.t: Just, therefore, is the doom which our Lord hath passed upon us. We shall surely taste it

37:32.t: We made you err, for we had erred ourselves

37:33.t: Partners therefore shall they be in punishment on that day

37:34.t: Truly, thus will we deal with the wicked

37:35.t: Because when it was said to them, There is no God but God, they swelled with pride

37:36.t: And said, "Shall we then abandon our gods for a crazed poet

37:37.t: Nay, he cometh with truth and confirmeth the Sent Ones of old

37:38.t: Ye shall surely taste the painful punishment

37:39.t: And ye shall not be rewarded but as ye have wrought

37:40.t: Save the sincere servants of God

37:41.t: A stated banquet shall they have

37:42.t: Of fruits; and honoured shall they be

37:45.t: A cup shall be borne round among them from a fountain

37:46.t: Limpid, delicious to those who drink

37:47.t: It shall not oppress the sense, nor shall they therewith be drunken

37:48.t: And with them are the large-eyed ones with modest refraining glances

37:50.t: And they shall address one another with mutual questions

37:51.t: Saith one of them, "I truly had a bosom friend

37:52.t: Who said, 'Art thou of those who credit it

37:53.t: What! when we shall have died, and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be judged

37:54.t: He shall say to those around him, "Will ye look

37:55.t: And he shall look and see him in the midst of Hell

37:56.t: And he shall say to him, "By God, thou hadst almost caused me to perish

37:57.t: And, but for the favour of my Lord, I had surely been of those who have been brought with thee into torment

37:58.t: But do we not die," say the blessed

37:59.t: Any other than our first death? and have we escaped the torment

37:60.t: This truly is the great felicity

37:61.t: For the like of this should the travailers travail

37:62.t: Is this the better repast or the tree Ez-zakkoum

37:63.t: Verily, we have made it for a subject of discord to the wicked

37:64.t: It is a tree which cometh up from the bottom of hell

37:65.t: Its fruits is as it were the heads of Satans

37:66.t: And, lo! the damned shall surely eat of it and fill their bellies with it

37:67.t: Then shall they have, thereon, a mixture of boiling water

37:68.t: Then shall they return to hell

37:70.t: And they hastened on in their footsteps

37:71.t: Also before them the greater number of the ancients had erred

37:72.t: Though we had sent warners among them

37:73.t: But see what was the end of these warned ones

37:75.t: Noah called on us of old, and right prompt were we to hear him

37:76.t: And we saved him and his family out of the great distress
