46:4.t: SAY: What think ye? As for those whom ye invoke beside God, shew me what part of the earth it is which they have created? Had they a share in the Heavens? Bring me a Book sent down by them before this Koran, or traces of their knowledge; - if ye are men of truth

46:5.t: And who erreth more than he who, beside God, calleth upon that which shall not answer him until the day of Resurrection? Yes, they regard not their invocations

46:6.t: And when mankind shall be assembled together, they will become their enemies, and ungratefully disown their worship

46:7.t: And when our clear signs are recited to them, they who believe not say of the truth when it cometh to them, "This is plain sorcery

46:8.t: Will they say, "He hath devised It?" SAY: If I have devised the Koran, then not one single thing shall ye ever obtain for me from God! He best knoweth what ye utter in its regard! Witness enough is He between me and you! And He is the Gracious, the Merciful

46:9.t: SAY: I am no apostle of new doctrines: neither know I what will be done with me or you. Only what is revealed to me do I follow, and I am only charged to warn openly

46:10.t: SAY: What think ye? If this Book be from God, and ye believe it not, and a witness of the children of Israel witness to its conformity with the Law, and believe, while ye proudly disdain it...? Ah! God guideth not the people guilty of such a wrong

46:11.t: But the infidels say of the believers, "If it were a good Book they would not have been before us in believing it:" And not having submitted to guidance, they proceed to say, "It is an old lying legend

46:12.t: But before the Koran was the Book of Moses, a rule and a mercy; and this Book confirmeth it
- in the Arabic tongue - that those who are guilty of that wrong may be warned, and as glad tidings to the doers of good

46:13.t: Assuredly they who say, "Our Lord is God," and take the straight way to Him - no fear shall come on them, neither shall they be put to grief

46:14.t: These shall be the inmates of Paradise to remain therein for ever, - the recompense of their deeds

46:15.t: Moreover, we have enjoined on man to shew kindness to his parents. With pain his mother beareth him; with pain she bringeth him forth: and his bearing and his weaning is thirty months; until when he attaineth his strength, and attaineth to forty years, he saith, "O my Lord! stir me up to be grateful for thy favours wherewith thou hast favoured me and my parents, and to do good works which shall please thee: and prosper me in my offspring: for to thee am I turned, and am resigned to thy will"

46:16.t: These are they from whom we will accept their best works, and whose evil works we will pass by; among the inmates shall they be of Paradise: - a true promise which they are promised

46:17.t: But he who saith to his parents, "Fie on you both! Promise ye me that I shall be taken forth from the grave alive, when whole generations have already passed away before me?" But they both will implore the help of God, and say, "Alas for thee! Believe: for the promise of God is true." But he saith, "It is no more than a fable of the ancients

46:18.t: These are they in whom the sentence passed on the nations, djinn and men, who flourished before them, is made good. They shall surely perish

46:19.t: And there are grades for all, according to their works, that God may repay them for their works; and they shall not be dealt with unfairly

46:20.t: And they who believe not shall one day be set before the fire. "Ye made away your precious gifts during your life on earth; and ye took your fill of pleasure in them: This day, therefore, with punishment of shame shall ye be rewarded, for that ye behaved you proudly and unjustly on the earth, and for that ye were given to excesses

46:21.t: Remember, too, the brother of Ad when he warned his people in AL AHKAF - and before and since his time there have been warners - "Worship none but God: verily I fear for you the punishment of the great day

46:22.t: They said, "Art thou come to us to turn us away from our gods? Bring on us now the woes which thou threatenest if thou speakest truth

46:23.t: That knowledge," said he, "is with God alone: I only proclaim to you the message with which I am sent. But I perceive that ye are a people sunk in ignorance

46:24.t: So when they saw a cloud coming straight for their valleys, they said, "It is a passing cloud that shall give us rain." "Nay, it is that whose speedy coming ye challenged a blast wherein is an afflictive punishment

46:25.t: It will destroy everything at the bidding of its Lord!" And at morn nought was to be seen but their empty dwellings! Thus repay we a wicked people

46:26.t: With power had we endued them, even as with power have we endued you; and we had given them ears and eyes and hearts: yet neither their eyes, nor their ears, nor their hearts aided them at all, when once they gainsaid the signs of God; but that punishment which they had mocked at enveloped them on all sides

46:27.t: Of old, too, did we destroy the cities which were round about you; and, in order that they might return to us, we varied our signs before them

46:28.t: But did those whom they took for gods beside God as his kindred deities, help them? Nay, they withdrew from them. Such was their delusion, and their device

46:29.t: And remember when we turned aside a company of the djinn to thee, that they might hearken to the Koran: and no sooner were they present at its reading than they said to each other, "Hist;" and when it was ended, they returned to their people with warnings

46:30.t: They said, "O our people! verily we have been listening to a book sent down since the days of Moses, affirming the previous scriptures; it guideth to the truth, and to the right way

46:31.t: O our people! Obey the Summoner of God, and believe in him, that He may forgive your sins, and rescue you from an afflictive punishment

46:32.t: And he who shall not respond to God's preacher, yet cannot weaken God's power on earth, nor shall he have protectors beside Him. These are in obvious error

46:33.t: See they not that God who created the Heavens and the Earth, and was not wearied with their creation, is of power to quicken the dead? Yea, he is for all things Potent

46:34.t: And a day is coming when the infidels shall be set before the fire. "Is not this it in truth?" They shall say, "Aye, by our Lord." He said, "Taste then the punishment for that ye would not believe

46:35.t: Bear thou up, then, with patience, as did the Apostles endued with firmness, and seek not to accelerate their doom. For, on the day when they shall see that with which they have been menaced, It shall be as though they had waited but an hour of the day. Enough! shall any perish save they who transgress

47:1.t: WHOSO believe not, and prevent others from the way of God - their works will He cause to miscarry

47:2.t: But whoso believe, and do things that are right, and believe in what hath been sent down to MUHAMMAD - for it is the truth from their Lord - their sins will He cancel, and dispose their hearts aright

47:3.t: This - because the infidels followed vanity, while those who believe, followed the truth from their Lord. Thus to men doth God set forth their likenesses

47:4.t: When ye encounter the infidels, strike off their heads till ye have made a great slaughter among them, and of the rest make fast the fetters. And afterwards let there either be free dismissals or ransomings, till the war hath laid down its burdens. Thus do. Were such the pleasure of God, he could himself take vengeance upon them: but He would rather prove the one of you by the other. And whoso fight for the cause of God, their works he will not suffer to miscarry

47:5.t: He will vouchsafe them guidance, and dispose their hearts aright

47:6.t: And he will bring them into the Paradise, of which he hath told them

47:7.t: Believers! if ye help God, God will help you, and will set your feet firm

47:8.t: But as for the infidels, let them perish: and their works shall God bring to nought

47:9.t: This - because they were averse from the command which God sent down; Fruitless, therefore, shall their works become

47:10.t: Have they not journeyed through the land, and seen what hath been the end of those who flourished before them? God brought destruction on them: and the like of this doth await the infidels

47:11.t: This - because God is the protector of those who believe, and because the infidels have no protector

47:12.t: Verily God will bring those who believe, and do the things that are right, into the Gardens, beneath whose shades the rivers flow: but they who believe not, take their fill, and eat as the beasts eat! And their dwelling-place the fire

47:13.t: And how many cities were mightier in strength than thy city, which hath thrust thee forth! We destroyed them, and there was none to help them

47:14.t: Shall he who followeth the clear teaching of his Lord be as he, the evil of whose doings hath been made to seem good to him, or like those who follow their own lusts

47:15.t: A picture of the Paradise which is promised to the God-fearing! Therein are rivers of water, which corrupt not: rivers of milk, whose taste changeth not: and rivers of wine, delicious to those who quaff it; And rivers of honey clarified: and therein are all kinds of fruit for them from their Lord! Is this like the lot of those who must dwell for ever in the fire? and shall have draughts of boiling water forced on them which will rend their bowels asunder

47:16.t: Some of them indeed hearken to thee, until when they go out from thee, they say with sneers to those to whom "the knowledge" hath been given, "What is this he said?" These are they whose hearts God hath sealed up, and who follow their own lusts

47:17.t: But as to those who have the guidance, He will increase their guidance, and He will teach them what to fear

47:18.t: For what do the infidels wait, but that the Hour come suddenly on them? Already are its signs come, and when it hath come on them indeed, how can they be warned then

47:19.t: Know, then, that there is no god but God: and ask pardon for thy sin, and for believers, both men and women. God knoweth your busy movements, and your final resting-places

47:20.t: The believers say, "Oh, would that a Sura were sent down!" but when a peremptory Sura is revealed, whose burden is war, thou mayest see the diseased of heart look toward thee, with a look of one on whom the shadows of death have fallen! But better in them would be obedience and becoming language

47:21.t: And if, when the command for war is issued, they are true to God, it will be assuredly best for them

47:22.t: Were ye not ready, if ye had turned back from Him, to spread disorder in the land, and violate the ties of blood

47:23.t: These are they whom God hath cursed, and made deaf, and blinded their eyes

47:24.t: Will they not then meditate on the Koran? Are locks upon their hearts

47:25.t: But as to those who return to their errors after "the guidance" hath been made plain to them, Satan shall beguile them, and fill them with his suggestions

47:26.t: This - because they say to those who abhor what God hath sent down, "We will comply with you in part of what ye enjoin." But God knoweth their secret reservations

47:27.t: But how? When the angels, in causing them to die, shall smite them on the face and back

47:28.t: This - because they follow that which angereth God, and abhor what pleaseth Him: therefore will He make their works fruitless

47:29.t: Think these men of diseased hearts, that God will not bring out their malice to light

47:30.t: If such were our pleasure, we could point them out to thee, and thou surely know them by their tokens: and know them thou shalt, by the strangeness of their words. God knoweth your doings

47:31.t: And we will surely test you, until we know the valiant and the steadfast among you: and we will test the reports of your conduct

47:32.t: Verily they who believe not, and turn others from the way of God, and separate from the Apostle after that "the guidance" hath been clearly shewn them, shall in no way injure God: but their works shall he bring to nought

47:33.t: Believers! obey God and the Apostle: and render not your works vain

47:34.t: Verily those who believe not, and who pervert others from the way of God, and then die in unbelief, God will not forgive

47:35.t: Be not fainthearted then; and invite not the infidels to peace when ye have the upper hand: for God is with you, and will not defraud you of the recompense of your works

47:36.t: Surely this present life is only a play, and pastime! but if ye believe, fear God; He will give you your rewards: but He will not ask all your riches of you

47:37.t: Should He ask them of you, and urge you, ye would shew yourself niggards: and He would bring your grudges to light

47:38.t: Lo! ye are they, who are called to expend for the cause of God: and some of you are niggards: but whoso is niggardly shall be niggard only to his own loss; for God is the Rich, and ye are the poor: and if ye turn back, He will change you for another people, and they shall not be your like

48:1.t: Verily, We have won for thee an undoubted VICTORY

48:2.t: In token that God forgiveth thy earlier and later faults, and fulfilleth His goodness to thee, and guideth thee on the right way

48:3.t: And that God succoureth thee with a mighty succour

48:4.t: He it is who sendeth down a spirit of secure repose into the hearts of the faithful that they might add faith to their faith;
for God's are the armies of the Heavens and of the Earth: and God is Knowing, Wise

48:5.t: And that He may bring the believing men and the believing women into gardens 'neath whose trees the rivers flow, to dwell therein for ever, and that He may cancel their evil deeds: for this is the great bliss with God

48:6.t: And that He may punish the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women, and the men and women who join other gods with God, and think evil thoughts of Him. Theirs shall be a round of evil; and God is angry with them and curseth them, and hath prepared Hell for them: and, an evil journey thither

48:7.t: The armies of the Heavens and of the Earth are God's, and God is Mighty, Wise

48:8.t: Verily, we have sent thee to be a witness and a herald of good

48:9.t: That ye may believe on God and on His Apostle; and may assist Him, and honour Him, and praise him, morning and evening

48:10.t: In truth, they who plighted fealty to thee, really plighted that fealty to God: the hand of God was over their hands! Whoever, therefore, shall break his oath shall only break it to his own hurt; but whoever shall be true to his engagement with God, He will give him a great reward

48:11.t: The Arabs who took not the field with you, will say to thee, "We were engaged with our property and our families; therefore ask thou pardon for us." They speak with their tongues what is not in their hearts. SAY: And who can have any power over God in your behalf, whether he will you some loss, or whether he will you an advantage? Yes, God is acquainted with your doings

48:12.t: But ye thought that the Apostle and the faithful could never more come back to their families; and your hearts were pleased at this; and ye thought an evil thought of this expedition, and ye became an undone people

48:13.t: For, whoso believeth not in God, and His Apostle.... Verily, we have got ready the flame for the Infidels

48:14.t: And God's is the kingdom of the Heavens and of the Earth: Whom He will He forgiveth, and whom He will He punisheth: and God is Gracious, Merciful

48:15.t: They who took not the field with you will say, when ye go forth to the spoil to take it, "Let us follow you." Fain would they change the word of God. SAY: Ye shall by no means follow us: thus hath God said already. They will say, "Nay, ye are jealous of us." Nay! they are men of little understanding

48:16.t: SAY to those Arabs of the desert, who took not the field, ye shall be called forth against a people of mighty valour. Ye shall do battle with them, or they shall profess Islam. If ye obey, a goodly recompense will God give you; but if ye turn back, as ye turned back aforetime, He will chastise you with a sore chastisement

48:17.t: It shall be no crime on the part of the blind, the lame, or the sick, if they go not to the fight. But whoso shall obey God and His Apostle, he shall bring him into the gardens 'neath which the rivers flow: but whoso shall turn back, He will punish him with a sore punishment

48:18.t: Well pleased now hath God been with the believers when they plighted fealty to thee under the tree; and He knew what was in their hearts: therefore did He send down upon them a spirit of secure repose, and rewarded them with a speedy victory

48:19.t: And with the rich booty which they took: for God is Mighty, Wise

48:20.t: God promised you the taking of a rich booty and sped it to you; and He withheld men's hands from you, for a sign to the faithful, and that He might guide you along the right way

48:21.t: And other booty, over which ye have not yet had power: but now hath God compassed them for you; for God is over all things Potent

48:22.t: If the Infidels shall fight against you, they shall assuredly turn their backs; then, neither protector nor helper shall they find

48:23.t: Such is God's method carried into effect of old; no change canst thou find in God's mode of dealing

48:24.t: And He it was who held their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca, after that He had given you the victory over them: for God saw what ye did

48:25.t: These are they who believed not, and kept you away from the sacred Mosque, as well as the offering which was prevented from reaching the place of sacrifice. And had it not been that ye would have trodden down believers, both men and women, whom ye knew not, so that a crime might have lighted on you without your knowledge on their account, and that God would bring whom He will within His mercy, this would have been otherwise ordered. Had they been apart, we had surely punished such of them as believed not, with a sore punishment

48:26.t: When the unbelievers had fostered rage in their hearts - the rage of ignorance
- God sent down His peace on His Apostle and on the faithful, and stablished in them the word of piety, for they were most worthy and deserving of it: and God knoweth all things

48:27.t: Now hath God in truth made good to His Apostle the dream in which he said, "Ye shall surely enter the sacred Mosque, if God will, in full security, having your heads shaved and your hair cut: ye shall not fear; for He knoweth what ye know not; and He hath ordained you, beside this, a speedy victory

48:28.t: It is He who hath sent His Apostle with "the Guidance," and the religion of truth, that He may exalt it above every religion. And enough for thee is this testimony on the part of God

48:29.t: Muhammad is the Apostle of God; and his comrades are vehement against the infidels, but full of tenderness among themselves. Thou mayst see them bowing down, prostrating themselves, imploring favours from God, and His acceptance. Their tokens are on their faces, the marks of their prostrations. This is their picture in the Law, and their picture in the Evangel: they are as the seed which putteth forth its stalk; then strengtheneth it, and it groweth stout, and riseth upon its stem, rejoicing the husbandman - that the infidels may be wrathful at them. To such of them as believe and do the things that are right, hath God promised forgiveness and a noble recompense

49:1.t: O BELIEVERS! enter not upon any affair ere God and His Apostle permit you; and fear ye God: for God Heareth, Knoweth

49:2.t: O Believers! raise not your voices above the voice of the Prophet, neither speak loud to him as ye speak loud one to another, lest your works come to nought, and ye unaware of it

49:3.t: They who lower their voices in the presence of the Apostle of God, are the persons whose hearts God hath inclined to piety. Forgiveness shall be theirs and a rich reward

49:4.t: They who call out to thee while thou art within thine APARTMENTS, have most of them no right perception of what is due to thee

49:5.t: But if they wait patiently till thou come forth to them, it were far better for them. But God is Indulgent, Merciful

49:6.t: O Believers! if any bad man come to you with news, clear it up at once, lest through ignorance ye harm others, and speedily have to repent of what ye have done

49:7.t: And know that an Apostle of God is among you! should he give way to you in many matters ye would certainly become guilty of a crime. But God hath endeared the faith to you, and hath given it favour in your hearts, and hath made unbelief, and wickedness, and disobedience hateful to you. Such are they who pursue a right course

49:8.t: Through the bounty and grace which is from God: and God is Knowing, Wise

49:9.t: If two bodies of the faithful are at war, then make ye peace between them: and if the one of them wrong the other, fight against that party which doth the wrong, until they come back to the precepts of God: if they come back, make peace between them with fairness, and act impartially; God loveth those who act with impartiality

49:10.t: Only the faithful are brethren; wherefore make peace between your brethren; and fear God, that ye may obtain mercy

49:11.t: O Believers! let not men laugh men to scorn who haply may be better than themselves; neither let women laugh women to scorn who may haply be better than themselves! Neither defame one another, nor call one another by nicknames. Bad is it to be called wicked after having professed the faith: and whoso repent not of this are doers of wrong

49:12.t: O Believers! avoid frequent suspicions, for some suspicions are a crime; and pry not: neither let the one of you traduce another in his absence. Would any one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? Surely ye would loathe it. And fear ye God: for God is Ready to turn, Merciful

49:13.t: O men! verily, we have created you of a male and a female; and we have divided you into peoples and tribes that ye might have knowledge one of another. Truly, the most worthy of honour in the sight of God is he who feareth Him most. Verily, God is Knowing, Cognisant

49:14.t: The Arabs of the desert say, "We believe." Say thou: Ye believe not; but rather say, "We profess Islam;" for the faith hath not yet found its way into your hearts. But if ye obey God and His Apostle, he will not allow you to lose any of your actions: for God is Indulgent, Merciful

49:15.t: The true believers are those only who believe in God and His Apostle, and afterwards doubt not; and who contend with their substance and their persons on the path of God. These are the sincere

49:16.t: SAY: Will ye teach God about your religion? when God knoweth whatever is in the Heavens and on the Earth: yea, God hath knowledge of all things

49:17.t: They taunt thee with their having embraced Islam. SAY: Taunt me not with your having embraced Islam: God rather taunteth you with His having guided you to the faith: acknowledge this if ye are sincere

49:18.t: Verily, God knoweth the secrets of the Heavens and of the Earth: and God beholdeth what ye do

50:2.t: They marvel forsooth that one of themselves hath come to them charged with warnings. "This," say the infidels, "is a marvellous thing

50:3.t: What! when dead and turned to dust shall we....? Far off is such a return as this

50:4.t: Now know we what the earth consumeth of them, and with us is a Book in which account is kept

50:5.t: But they have treated the truth which hath come to them as falsehood; perplexed therefore is their state

50:6.t: Will they not look up to the heaven above them, and consider how we have reared it and decked it forth, and that there are no flaws therein

50:7.t: And as to the earth, we have spread it out, and have thrown the mountains upon it, and have caused an upgrowth in it of all beauteous kinds of plants

50:8.t: For insight and admonition to every servant who loveth to turn to God

50:9.t: And we send down the rain from Heaven with its blessings, by which we cause gardens to spring forth and the grain of harvest

50:10.t: And the tall palm trees with date-bearing branches one above the other

50:11.t: For man's nourishment: And life give we thereby to a dead country. So also shall be the resurrection

50:12.t: the people of Noah, and the men of Rass and Themoud, treated their prophets as impostors

50:13.t: And Ad and Pharaoh, and the brethren of Lot

50:14.t: and the dwellers in the forest, and the people of Tobba, all gave the lie to their prophets: justly, therefore, were the menaces inflicted

50:15.t: Are we wearied out with the first creation? Yet are they in doubt with regard to a new creation

50:16.t: We created man: and we know what his soul whispereth to him, and we are closer to him than his neck-vein

50:17.t: When the two angels charged with taking account shall take it, one sitting on the right hand, the other on the left

50:18.t: Not a word doth he utter, but there is a watcher with him ready to note it down

50:19.t: And the stupor of certain death cometh upon him: "This is what thou wouldst have shunned

50:20.t: And there shall be a blast on the trumpet, - it is the threatened day

50:21.t: And every soul shall come, - an angel with it urging it along, and an angel to witness against it

50:22.t: Saith he, "Of this day didst thou live in heedlessness: but we have taken off thy veil from thee, and thy sight is becoming sharp this day

50:23.t: And he who is at this side shall say, "This is what I am prepared with against thee

50:24.t: And God will say, "Cast into Hell, ye twain, every infidel, every hardened one

50:25.t: The hinderer of the good, the transgressor, the doubter

50:26.t: Who set up other gods with God. Cast ye him into the fierce torment

50:27.t: He who is at his side shall say, "O our Lord! I led him not astray, yet was he in an error wide of truth

50:28.t: He shall say, "Wrangle not in my presence. I had plied you beforehand with menaces

50:29.t: My doom changeth not, and I am not unjust to man

50:30.t: On that day will we cry to Hell, "Art thou full?" And it shall say, "Are there more

50:31.t: And not far from thence shall Paradise be brought near unto the Pious

50:32.t: This is what ye have been promised: to every one who hath turned in penitence to God and kept his laws

50:33.t: Who hath feared the God of Mercy in secret, and come to him with a contrite heart

50:34.t: Enter it in peace: this is the day of Eternity

50:35.t: There shall they have all that they can desire: and our's will it be to augment their bliss

50:36.t: And how many generations have we destroyed ere the days of these
, mightier than they in strength! Search ye then the land. Is there any escape

50:37.t: Lo! herein is warning for him who hath a heart, or giveth ear, and is himself an eye-witness

50:38.t: We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and no weariness touched us

50:39.t: Wherefore put up with what they say, and celebrate the praise of thy Lord before sunrise and before sunset

50:40.t: And praise Him in the night: and perform the two final prostrations

50:41.t: And list for the day whereon the crier shall cry from a place near to every one alike

50:42.t: The day on which men shall in truth hear that shout will be the day of their coming forth from the grave

50:43.t: Verily, we cause to live, and we cause to die. To us shall all return

50:44.t: On the day when the earth shall swiftly cleave asunder over the dead, will this gathering be easy to Us

50:45.t: We know best what the infidels say: and thou art not to compel them. Warn then by the Koran those who fear my menace

51:1.t: By the clouds which scatter with SCATTERING

51:2.t: And those which bear their load

51:3.t: And by those which speed lightly along

51:4.t: And those which apportion by command

51:5.t: True, indeed, is that with which ye are threatened

51:6.t: And lo! the judgment will surely come

51:8.t: Ye are discordant in what ye say

51:9.t: But whose turneth him from the truth, is turned from it by a divine decree

51:11.t: Who are bewildered in the depths of ignorance

51:12.t: They ask, "When this day of judgment

51:13.t: On that day they shall be tormented at the fire

51:14.t: Taste ye of this your torment, whose speedy coming ye challenged

51:15.t: But the God-fearing shall dwell amid gardens and fountains

51:16.t: Enjoying what their Lord hath given them, because, aforetime they were well-doers

51:17.t: But little of the night was it that they slept

51:18.t: And at dawn they prayed for pardon

51:19.t: And gave due share of their wealth to the suppliant and the outcast

51:20.t: On Earth are signs for men of firm belief

51:21.t: And also in your own selves: Will ye not then behold them

51:22.t: The Heaven hath sustenance for you, and it containeth that which you are promised

51:23.t: By the Lord then of the heaven and of the earth, I swear that this is the truth, even as ye speak yourselves

51:24.t: Hath the story reached thee of Abraham's honoured guests

51:25.t: When they went in unto him and said, "Peace!" he replied, "Peace: - they are strangers

51:26.t: And he went apart to his family, and brought a fatted calf

51:27.t: And set it before them. He said, "Eat ye not

51:28.t: And he conceived a fear of them. They said to him, "Fear not;" and announced to him a wise son

51:29.t: His wife came up with outcry: she smote her face and said, "What I, old and barren

51:30.t: They said, "Thus saith thy Lord. He truly is the Wise, the Knowing

51:31.t: Said he, "And what, O messengers, is your errand

51:32.t: They said, "To a wicked people are we sent

51:33.t: To hurl upon them stones of clay

51:34.t: Destined by thy Lord for men guilty of excesses

51:35.t: And we brought forth the believers who were in the city

51:36.t: But we found not in it but one family of Muslims

51:37.t: And signs we left in it for those who dread the afflictive chastisement

51:38.t: And in Moses: when we sent him to Pharaoh with manifest power

51:39.t: But relying on his forces he turned his back and said, "Sorcerer, or Possessed

51:40.t: So we seized him and his hosts and cast them into the sea; for of all blame was he worthy

51:41.t: And in Ad: when we sent against them the desolating blast

51:42.t: It touched not aught over which it came, but it turned it to dust

51:43.t: And in Themoud: when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for yet a while

51:44.t: But they rebelled against their Lord's command: so the tempest took them as they watched its coming

51:45.t: They were not able to stand upright, and could not help themselves

51:46.t: And we destroyed the people of Noah, before them; for an impious people were they

51:47.t: And the Heaven - with our hands have we built it up, and given it its expanse

51:48.t: And the Earth - we have stretched it out like a carpet; and how smoothly have we spread it forth

51:49.t: And of everything have we created pairs: that haply ye may reflect

51:50.t: Fly then to God: I come to you from him a plain warner

51:51.t: And set not up another god with God: I come to you from him a plain warner

51:52.t: Even thus came there no apostle to those who flourished before them, but they exclaimed, "Sorcerer, or Possessed

51:53.t: Have they made a legacy to one another of this scoff? Yes, they are a rebel people

51:54.t: Turn away, then, from them, and thou shalt not incur reproach

51:55.t: Yet warn them, for, in truth, warning will profit the believers

51:56.t: I have not created Djinn and men, but that they should worship me

51:57.t: I require not sustenance from them, neither require I that they feed me

51:58.t: Verily, God is the sole sustainer: possessed of might: the unshaken

51:59.t: Therefore to those who injure thee shall be a fate like the fate of their fellows of old. Let them not challenge me to hasten it

51:60.t: Woe then to the infidels, because of their threatened day

52:7.t: Verily, a chastisement from thy Lord is imminent

52:8.t: And none shall put it back

52:9.t: Reeling on that day the Heaven shall reel

52:10.t: And stirring shall the mountains stir

52:11.t: And woe, on that day, to those who called the apostles liars

52:12.t: Who plunged for pastime into vain disputes

52:13.t: On that day shall they be thrust with thrusting to the fire of Hell

52:14.t: This is the fire which ye treated as a lie

52:15.t: What! is this magic, then? or, do ye not see it

52:16.t: Burn ye therein: bear it patiently or impatiently 'twill be the same to you: for ye shall assuredly receive the reward of your doings

52:17.t: But mid gardens and delights shall they dwell who have feared God

52:18.t: Rejoicing in what their Lord hath given them; and that from the pain of hell-fire hath their Lord preserved them

52:19.t: Eat and drink with healthy enjoyment, in recompense for your deeds

52:20.t: On couches ranged in rows shall they recline; and to the damsels with large dark eyes will we wed them

52:21.t: And to those who have believed, whose offspring have followed them in the faith, will we again unite their offspring; nor of the meed of their works will we in the least defraud them. Pledged to God is every man for his actions and their desert

52:22.t: And fruits in abundance will we give them, and flesh as they shall desire

52:23.t: Therein shall they pass to one another the cup which shall engender no light discourse, no motive to sin

52:24.t: And youths shall go round among them beautiful as imbedded pearls

52:25.t: And shall accost one another and ask mutual questions

52:26.t: A time indeed there was," will they say, "when we were full of care as to the future lot of our families

52:27.t: But kind hath God been to us, and from the pestilential torment hath he preserved us

52:28.t: For, heretofore we called upon Him - and He is the Beneficent, the Merciful

52:29.t: Warn thou, then. For thou by the favour of thy Lord art neither soothsayer nor possessed

52:30.t: Will they say, "A poet! let us await some adverse turn of his fortune

52:31.t: SAY, wait ye, and in sooth I too will wait with you

52:32.t: Is it their dreams which inspire them with this? or is it that they are a perverse people

52:33.t: Will they say, "He hath forged it
himself?" Nay, rather it is that they believed not

52:34.t: Let them then produce a discourse like it, if they speak the Truth

52:35.t: Were they created by nothing? or were they the creators of themselves

52:36.t: Created they the Heavens and Earth? Nay, rather, they have no faith

52:37.t: Hold they thy Lord's treasures? Bear they the rule supreme

52:38.t: Have they a ladder for hearing the angels? Let any one who hath heard them bring a clear proof of it

52:39.t: Hath God daughters and ye sons

52:40.t: Asketh thou pay of them? they are themselves weighed down with debts

52:41.t: Have they such a knowledge of the secret things that they can write them down

52:42.t: Desire they to lay snares for thee? But the snared ones shall be they who do not believe

52:43.t: Have they any God beside God? Glory be to God above what they join with Him

52:44.t: And should they see a fragment of the heaven falling down, they would say, "It is only a dense cloud

52:45.t: Leave them then until they come face to face with the day when they shall swoon away

52:46.t: A day in which their snares shall not at all avail them, neither shall they be helped

52:47.t: And verily, beside this is there a punishment for the evildoers: but most of them know it not

52:48.t: Wait thou patiently the judgment of thy Lord, for thou art in our eye; and celebrate the praise of thy Lord when thou risest up

52:49.t: And in the night-season: Praise him when the stars are setting

53:1.t: By the STAR when it setteth

53:2.t: Your compatriot erreth not, nor is he led astray

53:3.t: Neither speaketh he from mere impulse

53:4.t: The Koran is no other than a revelation revealed to him

53:5.t: One terrible in power taught it him

53:6.t: Endued with wisdom. With even balance stood he

53:7.t: In the highest part of the horizon

53:8.t: Then came he nearer and approached

53:9.t: And was at the distance of two bows, or even closer

53:10.t: And he revealed to his servant what he revealed

53:11.t: His heart falsified not what he saw

53:12.t: What! will ye then dispute with him as to what he saw

53:13.t: He had seen him also another time

53:14.t: Near the Sidrah-tree, which marks the boundary

53:15.t: Near which is the garden of repose

53:16.t: When the Sidrah-tree was covered with what covered it

53:17.t: His eye turned not aside, nor did it wander

53:18.t: For he saw the greatest of the signs of his Lord

53:19.t: Do you see Al-Lat and Al-Ozza

53:20.t: And Manat the third idol besides

53:21.t: What? shall ye have male progeny and God female

53:22.t: This were indeed an unfair partition

53:23.t: These are mere names: ye and your fathers named them thus: God hath not sent down any warranty in their regard. A mere conceit and their own impulses do they follow. Yet hath "the guidance" from their Lord come to them

53:24.t: Shall man have whatever he wisheth

53:25.t: The future and the present are in the hand of God

53:26.t: And many as are the Angels in the Heavens, their intercession shall be of no avail Until God hath permitted it to whom he shall please and will accept

53:27.t: Verily, it is they who believe not in the life to come, who name the angels with names of females

53:28.t: But herein they have no knowledge: they follow a mere conceit; and mere conceit can never take the place of truth

53:29.t: Withdraw then from him who turneth his back on our warning and desireth only this present life

53:30.t: This is the sum of their knowledge. Truly thy Lord best knoweth him who erreth from his way, and He best knoweth him who hath received guidance

53:31.t: And whatever is in the Heavens and in the Earth is God's that he may reward those who do evil according to their deeds: and those who do good will He reward with good things

53:32.t: To those who avoid great crimes and scandals but commit only lighter faults, verily, thy Lord will be diffuse of mercy. He well knew you when he produced you out of the earth, and when ye were embryos in your mother's womb. Assert not then your own purity. He best knoweth who feareth him

53:33.t: Hast thou considered him who turned his back

53:34.t: Who giveth little and is covetous

53:35.t: Is it that he hath the knowledge and vision of the secret things

53:36.t: Hath he not been told of what is in the pages of Moses

53:37.t: And of Abraham faithful to his pledge

53:38.t: That no burdened soul shall bear the burdens of another

53:39.t: And that nothing shall be reckoned to a man but that for which he hath made efforts

53:40.t: And that his efforts shall at last be seen in their true light

53:41.t: That then he shall be recompensed with a most exact recompense

53:42.t: And that unto thy Lord is the term of all things

53:43.t: And that it is He who causeth to laugh and to weep

53:44.t: And that He causeth to die and maketh alive

53:45.t: And that He hath created the sexes, male and female

53:46.t: From the diffused germs of life

53:47.t: And that with Him is the second creation

53:48.t: And that He enricheth and causeth to possess

53:49.t: And that He is the Lord of Sirius

53:50.t: And that it was He who destroyed the ancient Adites

53:51.t: And the people of Themoud and left not one survivor

53:52.t: And before them the people of Noah who were most wicked and most perverse

53:53.t: And it was He who destroyed the cities that were overthrown

53:54.t: So that that which covered them covered them

53:55.t: Which then of thy Lord's benefits wilt thou make a matter of doubt

53:56.t: He who warneth you is one of the warners of old

53:57.t: The day that must draw nigh, draweth nigh already

53:58.t: and yet none but God can reveal its time

53:59.t: Is it at these sayings that ye marvel

53:60.t: And that ye laugh and weep not

53:62.t: Prostrate yourselves then to God and worship

54:1.t: The hour hath approached and the MOON hath been cleft

54:2.t: But whenever they see a miracle they turn aside and say, This is well-devised magic

54:3.t: And they have treated the prophets as impostors, and follow their own lusts; but everything is unalterably fixed

54:4.t: A message of prohibition had come to them

54:5.t: Consummate wisdom - but warners profit them not

54:6.t: Quit them then. On the day when the summoner shall summon to a stern business

54:7.t: With downcast eyes shall they come forth from their graves, as if they were scattered locusts

54:8.t: Hastening to the summoner. "This," shall the infidels say, "is the distressful day

54:9.t: Before them the people of Noah treated the truth as a lie. Our servant did they charge with falsehood, and said, "Demoniac!" and he was rejected

54:10.t: Then cried he to his Lord, "Verily, they prevail against me; come thou therefore to my succour

54:11.t: So we opened the gates of Heaven with water which fell in torrents

54:12.t: And we caused the earth to break forth with springs, and their waters met by settled decree

54:13.t: And we bare him on a vessel made with planks and nails

54:14.t: Under our eyes it floated on: a recompence to him who had been rejected with unbelief

54:15.t: And we left it a sign: but, is there any one who receives the warning

54:16.t: And how great was my vengeance and my menace

54:17.t: Easy for warning have we made the Koran - but, is there any one who receives the warning

54:18.t: The Adites called the truth a lie: but how great was my vengeance and my menace

54:19.t: For we sent against them a roaring wind in a day of continued distress

54:20.t: It tore men away as though they were uprooted palm stumps

54:21.t: And how great was my vengeance and my menace

54:22.t: Easy for warning have we made the Koran - but, is there any one who receives the warning

54:23.t: The tribe of Themoud treated the threatenings as lies

54:24.t: And they said, "Shall we follow a single man from among ourselves? Then verily should we be in error and in folly

54:25.t: To him alone among us is the office of warning entrusted? No! he is an impostor, an insolent person

54:26.t: To-morrow shall they learn who is the impostor, the insolent

54:27.t: For we will send the she-camel to prove them: do thou mark them well, O Saleh, and be patient

54:28.t: And foretell them that their waters shall be divided between themselves and her, and that every draught shall come by turns to them

54:29.t: But they called to their comrade, and he took a knife and ham-strung her

54:30.t: And how great was my vengeance and my menance

54:31.t: We sent against them a single shout; and they became like the dry sticks of the fold-builders

54:32.t: Easy have we made the Koran for warning - but, is there any one who receives the warning

54:33.t: The people of Lot treated his warning as a lie

54:34.t: But we sent a stone-charged wind against them all, except the family of Lot, whom at daybreak we delivered

54:35.t: By our special grace - for thus we reward the thankful

54:36.t: He, indeed, had warned them of our severity, but of that warning they doubted

54:37.t: Even this guess did they demand: therefore we deprived them of sight, And said, "Taste ye my vengeance and my menace

54:38.t: And in the morning a relentless punishment overtook them

54:40.t: Easy have we made the Koran for warning but, is there any one who receives the warning

54:41.t: To the people of Pharaoh also came the threatenings

54:42.t: All our miracles did they treat as impostures. Therefore seized we them as he only can seize, who is the Mighty, the Strong

54:43.t: Are your infidels, O Meccans, better men than these? Is there an exemption for you in the sacred Books

54:44.t: Will they say, "We are a host that lend one another aid

54:45.t: The host shall be routed, and they shall turn them back

54:46.t: But, that Hour is their threatened time, and that Hour shall be most severe and bitter

54:47.t: Verily, the wicked are sunk in bewilderment and folly

54:48.t: On that day they shall be dragged into the fire on their faces. "Taste ye the touch of Hell

54:49.t: All things have we created after a fixed decree

54:50.t: Our command was but one word, swift as the twinkling of an eye

54:51.t: Of old, too, have we destroyed the like of you - yet is any one warned

54:52.t: And everything that they do is in the Books

54:53.t: Each action, both small and great, is written down

54:54.t: Verily, amid gardens and rivers shall the pious dwell

54:55.t: In the seat of truth, in the presence of the potent King

55:5.t: The Sun and the Moon have each their times

55:6.t: And the plants and the trees bend in adoration

55:7.t: And the Heaven, He hath reared it on high, and hath appointed the balance

55:8.t: That in the balance ye should not transgress

55:9.t: Weigh therefore with fairness, and scant not the balance

55:10.t: And the Earth, He hath prepared it for the living tribes

55:11.t: Therein are fruits, and the palms with sheathed clusters

55:12.t: And the grain with its husk, and the fragrant plants

55:13.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny

55:14.t: He created man of clay like that of the potter

55:15.t: And He created the djinn of pure fire

55:16.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?
RODWELL: Which then of the bounties, etc

55:17.t: He is the Lord of the East, He is the Lord of the West

55:18.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:19.t: He hath let loose the two seas which meet each other

55:20.t: Yet between them is a barrier which they overpass not

55:21.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:22.t: From each he bringeth up pearls both great and small

55:23.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:24.t: And His are the ships towering up at sea like mountains

55:25.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:26.t: All on the earth shall pass away

55:27.t: But the face of thy Lord shall abide resplendent with majesty and glory

55:28.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:29.t: To Him maketh suit all that is in the Heaven and the Earth. Every day doth some new work employ Him

55:30.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:31.t: We will find leisure to judge you, O ye men and djinn

55:32.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:33.t: O company of djinn and men, if ye can overpass the bounds of the Heavens and the Earth, then overpass them. But by our leave only shall ye overpass them

55:34.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:35.t: A bright flash of fire shall be hurled at you both, and molten brass, and ye shall not defend yourselves from it

55:36.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:37.t: When the Heaven shall be cleft asunder, and become rose red, like stained leather

55:38.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:39.t: On that day shall neither man nor djinn be asked of his sin

55:40.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:41.t: By their tokens shall the sinners be known, and they shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet

55:42.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:43.t: This is Hell which sinners treated as a lie

55:44.t: To and fro shall they pass between it and the boiling water

55:45.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:46.t: But for those who dread the majesty of their Lord shall be two gardens

55:47.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:49.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:51.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:52.t: In each two kinds of every fruit

55:53.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:54.t: On couches with linings of brocade shall they recline, and the fruit of the two gardens shall be within easy reach

55:55.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:56.t: Therein shall be the damsels with retiring glances, whom nor man nor djinn hath touched before them

55:57.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:59.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:60.t: Shall the reward of good be aught but good

55:61.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:62.t: And beside these shall be two other gardens

55:63.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:65.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:67.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:68.t: In each, fruits and the palm and the pomegranate

55:69.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:70.t: In each, the fair, the beauteous ones

55:71.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:72.t: With large dark eyeballs, kept close in their pavilions

55:73.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:74.t: Whom man hath never touched, nor any djinn

55:75.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:76.t: Their spouses on soft green cushions and on beautiful carpets shall recline

55:77.t: Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye twain deny?

55:78.t: Blessed be the name of thy Lord, full of majesty and glory

56:1.t: WHEN the day that must come shall have come suddenly

56:2.t: None shall treat that sudden coming as a lie

56:3.t: Day that shall abase! Day that shall exalt

56:4.t: When the earth shall be shaken with a shock

56:5.t: And the mountains shall be crumbled with a crumbling

56:7.t: And into three bands shall ye be divided

56:8.t: Then the people of the right hand - Oh! how happy shall be the people of the right hand

56:9.t: And the people of the left hand - Oh! how wretched shall be the people of the left hand

56:10.t: And they who were foremost on earth - the foremost still

56:11.t: These are they who shall be brought nigh to God

56:14.t: And few of the latter generations

56:16.t: Reclining on them face to face

56:17.t: Aye-blooming youths go round about to them

56:18.t: With goblets and ewers and a cup of flowing wine

56:19.t: Their brows ache not from it, nor fails the sense

56:20.t: And with such fruits as shall please them best

56:21.t: And with flesh of such birds, as they shall long for

56:22.t: And theirs shall be the Houris, with large dark eyes

56:23.t: like pearls hidden in their shells

56:24.t: In recompense of their labours past

56:25.t: No vain discourse shall they hear therein, nor charge of sin

56:27.t: And the people of the right hand - oh! how happy shall be the people of the right hand

56:29.t: And tall trees clad with fruit

56:35.t: Of a rare creation have we created the Houris

56:36.t: And we have made them ever virgins

56:37.t: Dear to their spouses, of equal age with them

56:38.t: For the people of the right hand

56:40.t: And a crowd of the latter generations

56:41.t: But the people of the left hand - oh! how wretched shall be the people of the left hand

56:42.t: Amid pestilential winds and in scalding water

56:43.t: And in the shadow of a black smoke

56:44.t: Not cool, and horrid to behold

56:45.t: For they truly, ere this, were blessed with worldly goods

56:47.t: And were wont to say, "What! after we have died, and become dust and bones, shall we be raised

56:48.t: And our fathers, the men of yore

56:49.t: SAY: Aye, the former and the latter

56:50.t: Gathered shall they all be for the time of a known day

56:51.t: Then ye, O ye the erring, the gainsaying

56:52.t: Shall surely eat of the tree Ez-zakkoum

56:53.t: And fill your bellies with it

56:54.t: And thereupon shall ye drink boiling water

56:55.t: And ye shall drink as the thirsty camel drinketh

56:56.t: This shall be their repast in the day of reckoning

56:57.t: We created you, will ye not credit us

56:58.t: What think ye? The germs of life

56:59.t: Is it ye who create them? or are we their creator

56:60.t: It is we who have decreed that death should be among you

56:61.t: Yet are we not thereby hindered from replacing you with others, your likes, or from producing you again in a form which ye know not

56:62.t: Ye have known the first creation: will ye not then reflect

56:63.t: What think ye? That which ye sow

56:64.t: Is it ye who cause its upgrowth, or do we cause it to spring forth

56:65.t: If we pleased we could so make your harvest dry and brittle that ye would ever marvel and say

56:66.t: Truly we have been at cost

56:68.t: What think ye of the water ye drink

56:69.t: Is it ye who send it down from the clouds, or send we it down

56:70.t: Brackish could we make it, if we pleased: will ye not then be thankful

56:71.t: What think ye? The fire which ye obtain by friction

56:72.t: Is it ye who rear its tree, or do we rear it

56:73.t: It is we who have made it for a memorial and a benefit to the wayfarers of the desert

56:74.t: Praise therefore the name of thy Lord, the Great

56:75.t: It needs not that I swear by the setting of the stars

56:76.t: And it is a great oath, if ye knew it

56:77.t: That this is the honourable Koran

56:79.t: Let none touch it but the purified

56:80.t: It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds

56:81.t: Such tidings as these will ye disdain

56:82.t: Will ye make it your daily bread to gainsay them

56:83.t: Why, at the moment when the soul of a dying man shall come up into his throat

56:84.t: And when ye are gazing at him

56:85.t: Though we are nearer to him than ye, although ye see us not

56:86.t: Why do ye not, if ye are to escape the judgment

56:87.t: Cause that soul to return? Tell me, if ye speak the truth

56:88.t: But as to him who shall enjoy near access to God

56:89.t: His shall be repose, and pleasure, and a garden of delights

56:90.t: Yea, for him who shall be of the people of the right hand

56:91.t: Shall be the greeting from the people of the right hand - "Peace be to thee

56:92.t: But for him who shall be of those who treat the prophets as deceivers, And of the erring

56:93.t: His entertainment shall be of scalding water

56:95.t: Verily this is a certain truth

56:96.t: Praise therefore the name of thy Lord, the Great

57:1.t: ALL that is in the Heavens and in the Earth praiseth God, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

57:2.t: His the Kingdom of the Heavens and of the Earth; He maketh alive and killeth; and He hath power over all things

57:3.t: He is the first and the last; the Seen and the Hidden; and He knoweth all things

57:4.t: It is He who in six days created the Heavens and the Earth, then ascended His throne. He knoweth that which entereth the earth, and that which goeth forth from it, and what cometh down from Heaven, and what mounteth up to it; and wherever ye are, He is with you; and God beholdeth all your actions

57:5.t: His the kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth; and to God shall all things return

57:6.t: He causeth the night to pass into the day, and He causeth the day to pass into the night: and He knoweth the very secrets of the bosom

57:7.t: Believe in God and his apostle, and bestow in alms of that whereof God hath made you heirs: for whoever among you believe and give alms - their's shall be a great recompense

57:8.t: What hath come to you that ye believe not in God, although the apostle exhorteth you to believe in your Lord, and He hath accepted your alliance - if ye are true believers

57:9.t: He it is who hath sent down clear tokens upon His servant, that He may bring you out of darkness into light; and truly, Kind, Merciful to you is God

57:10.t: And what hath come to you that ye expend not for the cause of God? since the heritage of the Heavens and of the Earth is God's only! Those among you who contributed before the victory, and fought, shall be differently treated from certain others among you! Such shall have a nobler grade than those who contributed and fought after it. But a goodly recompense hath God promised to all; and God is fully informed of your actions

57:11.t: Who is he that will lend a generous loan to God? So will He double it to him, and he shall have a noble reward

57:12.t: One day thou shalt see the believers, men and women, with their light running before them, and on their right hand. The angels shall say to them, "Good tidings for you this day of gardens beneath whose shades the rivers flow, in which ye shall abide for ever!" This the great bliss

57:13.t: On that day the hypocrites, both men and women, shall say to those who believe, "Tarry for us, that we may kindle our light at yours." It shall be said, "Return ye back, and seek light for yourselves." But between them shall be set a wall with a gateway, within which shall be the Mercy, and in front, without it, the Torment

57:14.t: They shall cry to them, "Were we not with you?" They shall say, "Yes! but ye led yourselves into temptation, and ye delayed, and ye doubted, and the good things ye craved deceived you, till the doom of God arrived: - and the deceiver deceived you in regard to God

57:15.t: On that day, therefore, no ransom shall be taken from you or from those who believe not: - your abode the fire! - This shall be your master! and wretched the journey thither

57:16.t: Hath not the time come, for those who believe, to humble their hearts at the warning of God and at the truth which he hath sent down? and that they be not as those to whom the Scriptures were given heretofore, whose lifetime was prolonged, but whose hearts were hardened, and many of them were perverse

57:17.t: Know that God quickeneth the earth after its death! Now have we made these signs clear to you, that ye may understand

57:18.t: Verily, they who give alms, both men and women, and they who lend a generous loan to God, - doubled shall it be to them - and they shall have a noble recompense

57:19.t: And they who believed in God and his apostle are the men of truth, and the witnesses in the presence of their Lord; They shall have their recompense and their light: But as for the infidels, and those who give the lie to our signs, these shall be the inmates of Hell

57:20.t: Know ye that this world's life is only a sport, and pastime, and show, and a cause of vainglory among you! And the multiplying of riches and children is like the plants which spring up after rain - Their growth rejoiceth the husband-man; then they wither away, and thou seest them all yellow; then they become stubble. And in the next life is a severe chastisement, Or else pardon from God and His satisfaction: and this world's life is but a cheating fruition

57:21.t: Vie in hasting after pardon from your Lord, and Paradise - whose outspread is as the outspread of the Heaven and of the Earth: Prepared is it for those who believe in God and His apostles: Such is the bounty of God: to whom He will He giveth it: and of immense bounty is God

57:22.t: No mischance chanceth either on earth or in your own persons, but ere we created them, it was in the Book; - for easy is this to God

57:23.t: Lest ye distress yourselves if good things escape you, and be over joyous for what falleth to your share. God loveth not the presumptuous, the boaster

57:24.t: Who are covetous themselves and incite others to covetousness. But whose turneth away from almsgiving - Ah! God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy

57:25.t: We have sent our apostles with the clear tokens, and we have caused the Book and the balance to descend with them, that men might observe fairness. And we have sent down IRON. Dire evil resideth in it, as well as advantage, to mankind! God would know who will assist Him and his apostle in secret. Verily, God is Powerful, Strong

57:26.t: And of old sent we Noah and Abraham, and on their seed conferred the gift of prophecy, and the Book; and some of them we guided aright; but many were evil doers

57:27.t: Then we caused our apostles to follow in their footsteps; and we caused Jesus the son of Mary to follow them; and we gave him the Evangel, and we put into the hearts of those who followed him kindness and compassion: but as to the monastic life, they invented it themselves. The desire only of pleasing God did we prescribe to them, and this they observed not as it ought to have been observed: but to such of them as believed gave we their reward, though many of them were perverse

57:28.t: O ye who believe! fear God and believe in his apostle: two portions of his mercy will He give you. He will bestow on you light to walk in, and He will forgive you: for God is Forgiving, Merciful

57:29.t: That the people of the Book may know that they have no control over aught of the favours of God, and that these gifts of grace are in the hands of God, and that He vouchsafeth them to whom he will; for God is of immense bounty

58:1.t: God hath heard the words of HER WHO PLEADED with thee against her husband, and made her plaint to God; and God hath heard your mutual intercourse: for God Heareth, Beholdeth

58:2.t: As to those of you who put away their wives by saying, "Be thou to me as my mother's back" their mothers they are not; they only are their mothers who gave them birth! they certainly say a blameworthy thing and an untruth: But truly, God is Forgiving, Indulgent

58:3.t: And those who thus put away their wives, and afterwards would recall their words, must free a captive before they can come together again. To this are ye warned to conform: and God is aware of what ye do

58:4.t: And he who findeth not a captive to set free, shall fast two months in succession before they two come together. And he who shall not be able to do so, shall feed sixty poor men. This, that he may believe in God and His Apostle. These are the statutes of God: and for the unbelievers is an afflictive chastisement

58:5.t: Truly they who oppose God and His Apostle shall be brought low, as those who were before them were brought low. And now have we sent down demonstrative signs: and, for the Infidels is a shameful chastisement

58:6.t: On the day when God shall raise them all to life, and shall tell them of their doings. God hath taken count of them, though they have forgotten them! and God is witness over all things

58:7.t: Dost thou not see that God knoweth all that is in the Heavens and all that is in the Earth? Three persons speak not privately together, but He is their fourth; nor five, but He is their sixth; nor fewer nor more, but wherever they be He is with them. Then on the day of resurrection He will tell them of their deeds: for God knoweth all things

58:8.t: Hast thou not marked those who have been forbidden secret talk, and return to what they have been forbidden, and talk privately together with wickedness, and hate, and disobedience towards the Apostle? And when they come to thee, they greet thee not as God greeteth thee: and they say among themselves, "Why doth not God punish us for what we say?" Hell shall be their meed: they shall be burned at its fire: and a wretched passage thither

58:9.t: O Believers! when ye hold private converse together, let it not be with wickedness, and hate, and disobedience towards the Apostle; but let your private talk be with justice and the fear of God: aye, fear ye God unto whom ye shall be gathered

58:10.t: Only of Satan is this clandestine talk, that he may bring the faithful to grief: but, unless by God's permission, not aught shall he harm them! in God then let the faithful trust

58:11.t: O ye who believe! when it is said to you, "Make room in your assemblies," then make ye room. God will make room for you in Paradise! And when it is said to you, "Rise up," then rise ye up. God will uplift those of you who believe, and those to whom "the Knowledge" is given, to lofty grades! and God is cognisant of your actions

58:12.t: O ye who believe! when ye go to confer in private with the Apostle, give alms before such conference. Better will this be for you, and more pure. But if ye have not the means, then truly God is Lenient, Merciful

58:13.t: Do ye hesitate to give alms previously to your private conference? Then if ye do it not
and God will excuse it in you
, at least observe prayer, and pay the stated impost, and obey God and His Apostle: for God is cognisant of your actions

58:14.t: Hast thou not remarked those who make friends of that people with whom God is angered? They are neither of your party nor of theirs; and they swear to a lie, knowing it to be such

58:15.t: God hath got ready for them a severe torment: for, evil is that they do

58:16.t: They make a cloak of their faith, and turn others aside from the way of God: wherefore a shameful torment awaiteth them

58:17.t: Not at all shall their wealth or their children avail them aught against God. Companions shall they be of the fire: they shall abide therein for ever

58:18.t: On the day when God shall raise them all, they will swear to Him as they now swear to you, deeming that it will avail them. Are they not - yes they - the liars

58:19.t: Satan hath gotten mastery over them, and made them forget the remembrance of God. These are Satan's party. What! shall not verily the party of Satan be for ever lost

58:20.t: Verily, they who oppose God and His Apostle shall be among the most vile

58:21.t: God hath written this decree: "I will surely prevail, and my Apostles also." Truly God is Strong, Mighty

58:22.t: Thou shalt not find that any of those who believe in God, and in the last day, love him who opposeth God and His Apostle, even though they be their fathers, or their sons, or their brethren, or their nearest kin. On the hearts of these hath God graven the Faith, and with His own Spirit hath He strengthened them; and He will bring them into gardens, beneath whose shades the rivers flow, to remain therein eternally. God is well pleased in them, and they in Him. These are God's party! Shall not, of a truth, a party of God be for ever blessed

59:1.t: ALL that is in the Heavens and all that is on the Earth praiseth God! He, the Mighty, the Wise

59:2.t: He it is who caused the unbelievers among the people of the Book to quit their homes and join those who had EMIGRATED previously. Ye did not think that they would quit them; and they on their part thought that their fortresses would protect them against God: But God came upon them whence they looked not for Him, and cast such fear into their hearts that by their own hands as well as by the hands of the victorious believers they demolished their houses! Profit by this example ye who are men of insight

59:3.t: And were it not that God had decreed their exile, surely in this world would he have chastised them: but in the world to come the chastisement of the fire awaiteth them

59:4.t: This because they set them against God and his apostle; and whoso setteth him against God....! God truly is vehement in punishing

59:5.t: Your cutting down some of their palm trees and sparing others was by God's permission, and to put the wicked to shame

59:6.t: After the spoils of these Jews which God hath assigned to his apostle, ye pressed not with horse or camel. But God giveth his apostles power over what he will. God is Almighty

59:7.t: The spoil taken from the people of the towns and assigned by God to his apostle, belongeth to God, and to the apostle, and to his kindred, and to the orphan, and to the poor, and to the wayfarer, that none of it may circulate among such of you only as are rich: What the apostle hath given you, take: What he hath refused you, refuse: And fear ye God, for God is severe in punishing

59:8.t: also doth a part belong, who have been driven from their homes and their substance, and who seek favour from God and his goodwill, and aid God and his apostle. These are the men of genuine virtue

59:9.t: They of Medina who had been in possession of their abodes and embraced the faith before them, cherish those who take refuge with them; and they find not in their breasts any desire for what hath fallen to their share: they prefer them before themselves, though poverty be their own lot. And with such as are preserved from their own covetousness shall it be well

59:10.t: And they who have come after them into the faith say, "O our Lord! forgive us and our brethren who have preceded us in the faith, and put not into our hearts ill-will against those who believe. O our Lord! thou verily art Kind, Merciful

59:11.t: Hast thou not observed the disaffected saying to their unbelieving brethren among the people of the Book, "If ye be driven forth, we will go forth with you; and in what concerneth you, never will we obey any one; and if ye be attacked we will certainly come to your help." But God is witness that they are liars

59:12.t: No! if they were driven forth, they would not share their banishment; if they were attacked they would not help them, or if they help them they will surely turn their backs: then would they remain unhelped

59:13.t: Assuredly the fear of you is more intense in their hearts than the fear of God! This because they are a people devoid of discernment

59:14.t: will not fight against you in a body except in fenced towns or from behind walls. Mighty is their valour among themselves! thou thinkest them united - but their hearts are divided. This for that they are a people who understand not

59:15.t: They act like those who lately preceded them, who also tasted the result of their doings; and a grievous chastisement awaiteth them

59:16.t: Like Satan when he saith to a man, "Be an infidel:" and when he hath become an infidel, he saith, "I share not thy guilt: verily, I fear God the Lord of the Worlds

59:17.t: Of both, therefore, shall the end be that they dwell for ever in the fire: This is the recompense of the evil doers

59:18.t: O ye who believe! fear God. And let every soul look well to what it sendeth on before for the morrow. And fear ye God: Verily, God is cognisant of what ye do

59:19.t: And be ye not like those who forget God, and whom He hath therefore caused to forget their proper selves. Such men are the evil doers

59:20.t: The inmates of the Fire and the inmates of Paradise are not to be held equal. The inmates of Paradise only shall be the blissful

59:21.t: Had we sent down this Koran on some mountain, thou wouldst certainly have seen it humbling itself and cleaving asunder for the fear of God. Such are the parables we propose to men in order that they may reflect

59:22.t: He is God beside whom there is no god. He knoweth things visible and invisible: He is the Compassionate, the Merciful

59:23.t: He is God beside whom there is no god: He is the King, the Holy, the Peaceful, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Strong, the Most High! Far be the Glory of God from that which they unite with Him

59:24.t: He is God, the Producer, the Maker, the Fashioner! To Him are ascribed excellent titles. Whatever is in the Heavens and in the Earth praiseth Him. He is the Mighty, the Wise

60:1.t: O YE who believe! take not my foe and your foe for friends, shewing them kindness, although they believe not that truth which hath come to you: they drive forth the Apostles and yourselves because ye believe in God your Lord! If ye go forth to fight on my way, and from a desire to please me, and shew them kindness in private, I well know what ye conceal, and what ye discover! Whoso doth this hath already gone astray from the even way

60:2.t: If they meet with you they will prove your foes: hand and tongue will they put forth for your hurt, and will desire that you become infidels again

60:3.t: Neither your kindred nor your children shall at all avail you on the day of the resurrection. A severance between you will it make! and your actions doth God behold

60:4.t: A good example had ye in Abraham, and in those who followed him, when they said to their people, "Verily, we are clear of you, and of what ye worship beside God: we renounce you: and between us and hath hatred and enmity sprung up for ever, until ye believe in God alone." Yet imitate not the language of Abraham to his Father, "I will pray for thy forgiveness, but not aught shall I obtain for thee from God." O our Lord! in thee do we trust! to thee do we turn! to thee we shall come back at the last

60:5.t: O our Lord! expose us not for trial to the unbelievers, and forgive us: for thou art the Mighty, the Wise

60:6.t: A good example had ye in them, for all who hope in God and in the last day. But let who will turn back, God truly is the Rich, the Praiseworthy

60:7.t: God will, perhaps, establish good will between yourselves and those of them whom ye take to be your enemies: God is Powerful: and God is Gracious, Merciful

60:8.t: God doth not forbid you to deal with kindness and fairness toward those who have not made war upon you on account of your religion, or driven you forth from your homes: for God loveth those who act with fairness

60:9.t: Only doth God forbid you to make friends of those who, on account of your religion, have warred against you, and have driven you forth from your homes, and have aided those who drove you forth: and whoever maketh friends of them are wrong-doers

60:10.t: O Believers! when believing women come over to you as refugees

, then make TRIAL of them. God best knoweth their faith; but if ye have also ascertained their faith, let them not go back to the infidels; they are not lawful for them, nor are the unbelievers lawful for these women. But give them back what they have spent for their dowers. No crime shall it be in you to marry them, provided ye give them their dowers. Do not retain any right in the infidel women, but demand back what you have spent for their dowers, and let the unbelievers demand back what they have spent for their wives. This is the ordinance of God which He ordaineth among you: and God is Knowing, Wise

60:11.t: And if any of your wives escape from you to the Infidels from whom ye afterwards take any spoil, then give to those whose wives shall have fled away, the like of what they shall have spent for their dowers; and fear God in whom ye believe

60:12.t: O Prophet! when believing women come to thee, and pledge themselves that they will not associate aught with God, and that they will not steal or commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring scandalous charges, nor disobey thee in what is right, then plight thou thy faith to them, and ask pardon for them of God: for God is Indulgent, Merciful

60:13.t: O Believers! enter not into amity with those against whom God is angered; they despair of the life to come, even as the Infidels despair of the inmates of the tombs

61:1.t: ALL that is in the Heavens and all that is on the Earth praiseth God. He is the Mighty, the Wise

61:2.t: Believers! why profess ye that which ye practise not

61:3.t: Most hateful is it to God that ye say that which ye do not

61:4.t: Verily God loveth those who, as though they were a solid wall, do battle for his cause in serried lines

61:5.t: And bear in mind when Moses said to his people, "Why grieve ye me, O my people, when ye know that I am God's apostle unto you?" And when they went astray, God led their hearts astray; for God guideth not a perverse people

61:6.t: And remember when Jesus the son of Mary said, "O children of Israel! of a truth I am God's apostle to you to confirm the law which was given before me, and to announce an apostle that shall come after me whose name shall be Ahmad!" But when he
presented himself with clear proofs of his mission, they said, "This is manifest sorcery

61:7.t: But who more impious than he who when called to Islam deviseth a falsehood concerning God? God guideth not the wicked

61:8.t: Fain would they put out the light of God with their mouths! but though the Infidels hate it, God will perfect his light

61:9.t: He it is who hath sent his apostle with guidance and the religion of truth, that, though they hate it who join other gods with God, He may make it victorious over every other religion

61:10.t: O ye who believe! shall I shew you a merchandise that shall deliver you from the sore torment

61:11.t: Believe in God and his apostle, and do valiantly in the cause of God with your wealth and with your persons! This, did ye but know it, will be best for you

61:12.t: Your sins will He forgive you, and He will bring you into gardens beneath whose shades the rivers flow - into charming abodes in the gardens of Eden: This shall be the great bliss

61:13.t: And other things which ye desire will he bestow, Help from God and speedy conquest! Bear thou these tidings to the faithful

61:14.t: O ye who believe! be helpers

of God; as said Jesus the son of Mary to his apostles, "Who will come to the help of God?" "We," said the apostles, "will be helpers of God." And a part of the children of Israel believed, and a part believed not. But to those who believed gave we the upperhand over their foes, and soon did they prove victorious

62:1.t: ALL that is in the Heavens, and all that is on the Earth, uttereth the Praise of God, the King! the Holy! the Mighty! the Wise

62:2.t: It is He who hath sent to the pagan folk
an Apostle from among themselves, to rehearse His signs to them, and to purify them, and to impart to them a knowledge of "the Book" and wisdom; for aforetime were they in manifest error

62:3.t: And others among them have not yet overtaken those who preceded them in the faith. But He is the Mighty, the Wise

62:4.t: This is the goodness of God: He bestoweth it on whom He will: God is of immense goodness

62:5.t: They on whom the burden of the law was laid, and would not bear it, are like an ass beneath a load of books. A sorry likeness this, for the people who give the lie to the signs of God! God guideth not the people who do this wrong

62:6.t: SAY: O ye Jews, if ye profess that ye rather than other men are the friends of God, then wish for death if ye are men of truth

62:7.t: But never on account of their previous handywork will they wish for it, and God knoweth the wrong doers

62:8.t: SAY: Verily the death from which ye flee will surely meet you. Then shall ye be brought back to Him who knoweth alike the things done in secret and openly: and He will tell you of your actions

62:9.t: O ye who believe! When ye are summoned to prayer on the day of THE ASSEMBLY, haste to the commemoration of God, and quit your traffic. This, if ye knew it, will be best for you

62:10.t: And when the Prayer is ended, then disperse yourselves abroad and go in quest of the bounties of God; and, that it may be well with you, oft remember God

62:11.t: But when they get a sight of merchandise or sport, they disperse after it, and leave thee standing alone. SAY: God hath in reserve what is better than sport or wares. And God is the best provider

63:1.t: WHEN the Hypocrites come to thee, they say, "We bear witness that thou art the Sent One of God." God knoweth that thou art His Sent One: but God beareth witness that the HYPOCRITES do surely lie

63:2.t: Their faith have they used as a cloak, and they turn aside others from the way of God! Evil are all their doings

63:3.t: This, for that they believed, then became unbelievers!Therefore hath a seal been set upon their hearts, and they understand not
